title: LiveRamp Adds Meta to Cross-Media Intelligence
summary: LiveRamp expanded its Cross-Media Intelligence solution to enable cross-media measurement across Meta & other media channels, such as CTV, programmatic, social, and audio.
body_text: SAN FRANCISCO — LiveRamp (NYSE: RAMP), the leader in data collaboration, today announced it has expanded its Cross-Media Intelligence solution to enable cross-media measurement across Meta and other media channels, such as CTV, programmatic, social, and audio, enabling brand marketers to measure campaigns across more of their media investments in a single, unified view. Through Cross-Media Intelligence, marketers can unlock powerful insights by incorporating Meta campaign data into broader cross-media measurement workflows. Marketers can access de-duplicated attribution and incrementality measurement from Meta in the LiveRamp Clean Room, powering unified reporting based on first-party data. By connecting Meta campaign data with the rest of their media investments, marketers gain new cross-channel insights, including reporting that accommodates their preferred tactics, creative variations, and campaign objectives. As a result, marketers can optimize performance for more effective investments. “What’s been really valuable for Hill’s is to build the perspective which matters to us in our media strategy and breadth,” said Tarang Jain, Senior Director of Media at Hill’s Pet Nutrition. “If we want to see the reach, frequency, incrementality, or how a platform like Meta is performing best, we can go and do that. That is really valuable because we can’t get that slice of data anywhere else.” Leading brands including Hill’s Pet Nutrition have already begun measuring their campaigns in Cross-Media Intelligence. By connecting campaign data from Meta alongside their other media investments, these marketers have been able to build a more complete view of campaign performance, as well as make more informed, data-driven decisions across their media mix. “Cross-Media Intelligence was built to give brand marketers the single, trusted view of campaign performance that they’ve chased for so long, and now helps marketers to make informed decisions across Meta and other media,” said Christine Grammier, VP, Product at LiveRamp. “With Meta now available as a reporting source within Cross-Media Intelligence marketers can better understand campaign performance across more of their media mix using secure, interoperable workflows.” As marketers increasingly look to understand performance across fragmented channels and platforms, interoperable measurement workflows are becoming a growing priority across the advertising ecosystem. LiveRamp’s neutral clean room serves as the foundation for Cross-Media Intelligence, enabling publishers and brands to participate in measurement workflows while maintaining control over their underlying data. Through Cross-Media Intelligence, marketers gain a more complete and comparable view of campaign performance across channels, increasing demand for interoperable measurement approaches that extend beyond individual platforms. Reach out to info@liveramp.com to learn more. About LiveRamp LiveRamp is shaping the future of responsible data collaboration between the world’s leading brands, retailers, financial services providers, and healthcare innovators. As consumers embrace new AI-driven experiences, the LiveRamp data collaboration network exponentially expands the breadth and accuracy of the data on which marketing AI capabilities operate, powering deeper customer insight and measurable performance on a global scale. LiveRamp is headquartered in San Francisco, California, with offices worldwide. Learn more at LiveRamp.com . Contact PR@liveramp.com

title: Senate Contempt Resolution Against Anthony Fauci Sparks Debate Over Congressional Testimony

body_text: A new political dispute has emerged in Washington after Senator Rand Paul introduced a Senate contempt resolution involving Dr. Anthony Fauci’s appearance before a congressional committee. The controversy centers on Fauci’s decision to repeatedly invoke his Fifth Amendment right during testimony and whether that constitutional protection applied to the questions lawmakers asked. The matter has drawn strong reactions from both sides of the political spectrum. Supporters of the resolution argue that Congress has the authority to demand answers during investigations, while Fauci’s defenders maintain that his constitutional rights should be protected and that the hearing was politically motivated. As the Senate prepares to consider the resolution, the debate highlights broader questions about congressional oversight, executive pardons, constitutional protections, and accountability for public officials. Background: Fauci’s Congressional Testimony Dr. Anthony Fauci served as the director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) from 1984 until 2022 and became one of the most recognized public health officials in the United States during the COVID-19 pandemic. During a congressional hearing on July 29, Fauci delivered an opening statement before declining to answer lawmakers’ questions. According to reports, he invoked the Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination in response to every question posed to him. Senator Rand Paul, who chaired the hearing, argued that Fauci’s use of the Fifth Amendment was not justified. Paul claimed that questions focused on issues covered by a 2025 presidential pardon and therefore did not expose Fauci to potential criminal liability. Fauci, however, maintained that he was following legal advice from his attorneys and was exercising a constitutional protection available to him. What the Contempt Resolution Claims The proposed Senate resolution states that Fauci’s refusal to answer questions violated federal law governing responses to congressional subpoenas. According to the resolution, individuals summoned by Congress are required to provide relevant testimony unless a valid legal privilege applies. Senator Paul argued that Fauci’s refusal represented a failure to cooperate with a congressional investigation. He stated that the committee had warned Fauci about possible contempt proceedings but that Fauci continued declining to answer questions. The resolution recommends that federal prosecutors consider taking further action. However, legal experts often note that disputes involving congressional subpoenas and executive officials can involve complex constitutional questions. Whether a person’s refusal to testify constitutes contempt can depend on issues such as the scope of congressional authority, applicable privileges, and judicial interpretations. The Debate Over the Fifth Amendment The Fifth Amendment protects individuals from being forced to provide testimony that could potentially be used against them in a criminal case. Invoking this right is common in legal proceedings where a person believes answers could create legal exposure. Senator Paul argued that because of a previous pardon, Fauci could not face prosecution related to certain conduct covered by that pardon. Based on that argument, Paul said the Fifth Amendment protection did not apply. Fauci’s position was that his legal team advised him to invoke the amendment because of concerns surrounding the hearing and potential consequences of his answers. The disagreement reflects a larger constitutional debate about how pardons interact with Fifth Amendment protections and whether a pardon eliminates all possible risks associated with testimony. Questions Raised About COVID-19 Policies During the hearing, Senator Paul raised questions related to Fauci’s role during the COVID-19 pandemic. Paul referenced documents, including diary materials, that he said raised questions about Fauci’s private communications and public statements. Paul argued that certain statements in the documents suggested Fauci had significant influence over pandemic policies, including school closures and vaccine discussions. Fauci has previously defended his public health decisions and stated that his actions were based on available scientific information at the time. His supporters argue that criticism of his pandemic response often overlooks the challenges officials faced during an unprecedented global health emergency. The disagreement reflects continuing political divisions over how governments handled COVID-19 restrictions, vaccines, and public health guidance. Political Reactions From Both Parties The hearing revealed sharp differences between Republicans and Democrats. Republican lawmakers supporting the resolution argued that Congress has a responsibility to investigate government actions and that witnesses appearing under subpoena must provide answers. Democratic lawmakers defended Fauci’s career and criticized what they described as an effort to target a public health official for political reasons. Some Democrats argued that Fauci’s decades of public service should be considered when evaluating his actions. The disagreement demonstrates how investigations involving high-profile government officials often become part of broader political debates. What Happens Next The Senate committee is expected to review the contempt resolution before deciding whether to move forward. If approved, the matter could be referred for additional action. The outcome could influence future disputes between Congress and government officials regarding testimony, subpoenas, and constitutional protections. Regardless of the final decision, the case has renewed public attention on the balance between congressional oversight and individual legal rights. Conclusion The Senate contempt resolution involving Anthony Fauci has become a significant political and legal controversy. At its center is a disagreement over whether Fauci’s use of the Fifth Amendment during congressional testimony was legally justified. Supporters of Senator Rand Paul’s resolution argue that Congress must have the ability to obtain answers during investigations. Fauci’s supporters counter that constitutional protections should remain available even for former government officials. As the Senate considers the resolution, the debate is likely to continue raising important questions about accountability, constitutional rights, and the limits of congressional power. Sources NTD Television report, August 4, 2026. The Epoch Times report. It does not make independent legal conclusions or confirm allegations made by any individual or organization. Readers should consult official government documents, court records, and multiple reliable news sources for additional context.

title: Lyell Immunopharma Reports Business Highlights and Financial Results for the Second Quarter 2026
summary: PiNACLE pivotal clinical trial evaluating ronde-cel in 3L+ patients with LBCL on track to report additional data in second half of 2026, with pivotal data expected mid-2027 and BLA submission expected to follow in the second half of 2027 Presented updated ronde-cel data in more than 100 patients
body_text: Lyell Immunopharma Reports Business Highlights and Financial Results for the Second Quarter 2026 August 6, 2026 PDF Version PiNACLE pivotal clinical trial evaluating ronde-cel in 3L+ patients with LBCL on track to report additional data in second half of 2026, with pivotal data expected mid-2027 and BLA submission expected to follow in the second half of 2027 Presented updated ronde-cel data in more than 100 patients with relapsed/refractory LBCL at the EHA 2026 Congress, with Phase 1/2 safety data showing no Grade ≥ 3 CRS and low rates of Grade ≥ 3 ICANS supporting potential outpatient administration Reported updated LYL273 safety data in relapsed/refractory mCRC, with gastrointestinal prophylaxis regimen and standardized safety management plan reducing Grade ≥ 2 diarrhea or colitis from 55% to 10%; amended ongoing U.S. Phase 1 trial to a Phase 1/2 design to enable seamless expansion into a potential pivotal single-arm Phase 2 trial pending regulatory alignment Additional data from the U.S. Phase 1 trial of LYL273 in 3L+ patients with relapsed/refractory mCRC and End‑of-Phase 1 FDA meeting are expected in the second half of 2026 Approximately $228.0 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities as of June 30, 2026, expected to provide runway into Q3 2027 SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lyell Immunopharma, Inc. (Nasdaq: LYEL), a late-stage clinical company advancing a pipeline of next-generation chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapies for patients with cancer, today reported financial results and business highlights for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Second Quarter Updates and Recent Business Highlights Rondecabtagene Autoleucel (Ronde-cel): A next-generation dual-targeting CD19/CD20 CAR T-cell product candidate designed to increase complete response rates and prolong the duration of response as compared to approved CD19‑targeted CAR T-cell therapies for the treatment of large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) Ronde-cel is an autologous CAR T-cell product candidate under evaluation in two pivotal trials in patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) LBCL in the third- or later-line (3L+) setting (PiNACLE) and the second-line (2L) setting (PiNACLE‑H2H). Ronde-cel targets B cells that express either CD19 or CD20 with a true ‘OR’ logic gate to achieve full potency at either target and is manufactured with a process that enriches for CD62L-positive cells to generate more naïve and central memory CAR T cells with enhanced stemlike features and antitumor activity. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted ronde-cel Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) and Fast Track designations for the treatment of adults with R/R diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) in the 3L+ setting and also RMAT designation for the treatment of large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) in the 2L setting. The FDA has also granted ronde‑cel Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of DLBCL/HGBCL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements. In June 2026, Lyell presented updated safety data and translational insights for ronde-cel in two presentations at the European Hematology Association (EHA) 2026 Congress in Stockholm, Sweden. Safety data from more than 100 patients with R/R LBCL treated with ronde-cel (65 in the 3L+ setting and 43 in the 2L setting) were presented. There were no Grade ≥ 3 CRS events and low rates of Grade ≥ 3 ICANS reported in the Phase 1/2 trial as of the data cutoff date of May 5, 2026, supporting the potential for outpatient administration. The manufacturing success rate was 97%. Translational analyses were presented providing a biological basis for ronde-cel’s durable responses, including enhanced memory potential of cytotoxic effector cells from CD62L+ enrichment and CD19/CD20 dual-targeting to overcome low antigen expression. The PiNACLE pivotal single-arm trial, a seamless expansion of the 3L+ cohort in the Phase 1/2 multi‑cohort trial, is ongoing. Additional data from this trial are expected in the second half of 2026, and pivotal data are expected in mid-2027 with submission of a Biologics License Application (BLA) to the FDA expected to follow in the second half of 2027. The primary endpoint of the trial is overall response rate, including an evaluation of duration of response. PiNACLE-H2H, the first-of-its-kind Phase 3 randomized controlled trial evaluating ronde-cel versus investigator’s choice of axicabtagene ciloleucel or lisocabtagene maraleucel in patients with R/R LBCL in the 2L setting, continues to enroll patients. A progress update for this trial is expected in the second half of 2026. The trial’s primary endpoint is event-free survival. LYL273: A next-generation guanylyl cyclase C (GCC)-targeted CAR T-cell product candidate for the treatment of relapsed/refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) and other GCC-expressing cancers LYL273 is a GCC-targeted CAR T-cell product candidate enhanced with CD19 CAR expression and controlled cytokine release, designed to improve CAR T-cell expansion, immune cell infiltration and cancer cell killing in the hostile solid tumor microenvironment. In November 2025, Lyell acquired global rights (excluding mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan) to LYL273, which has shown promising dose-dependent clinical activity in patients with advanced R/R mCRC in a Phase 1 trial conducted in the U.S. following proof of concept in 15 patients in China. The FDA granted LYL273 Fast Track designation for the treatment of mCRC. In June 2026, Lyell reported updated safety data from patients with 3L+ R/R mCRC in the ongoing U.S. Phase 1 trial, including 19 patients, of which 10 were treated with gastrointestinal (GI) prophylaxis and a new safety management protocol and 9 were treated without GI prophylaxis across Dose Levels 1 and 2 (1 and 2 x 106 CAR+ cells/kg, respectively) as of the data cutoff date of May 5, 2026. The GI prophylaxis regimen included treatment with infliximab, vedolizumab and budesonide prior to the development of symptoms. The rate of Grade ≥ 2 diarrhea or colitis was reduced from 55% to 10%, and there were no reported cases of Grade ≥ 3 diarrhea or colitis in patients treated with GI prophylaxis. No patients treated with GI prophylaxis experienced Grade ≥ 3 CRS or ICANS. GCC CAR T-cell expansion kinetics were similar in patients treated with and without GI prophylaxis. Dose escalation continues, and the maximum tolerated dose has not been determined. Based on the new safety data, Lyell amended the ongoing U.S. Phase 1 trial to a Phase 1/2 design, enabling seamless expansion into a potential pivotal single-arm Phase 2 trial once the recommended Phase 2 dose is determined and subject to discussions with the FDA. The amendment adds new cohorts, including a 2L cohort and a cohort evaluating a combination strategy with radiotherapy. Additional U.S. Phase 1 clinical data in patients with R/R mCRC in the 3L+ setting and an End-of-Phase 1 meeting with the FDA are expected in the second half of 2026. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Lyell reported a net loss of $44.8 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $42.7 million for the same period in 2025. The $2.1 million increase in net loss was primarily due to a $4.7 million increase in research and development expenses driven by increased clinical trial activity and lower interest income, partially offset by lower property and equipment disposal losses, and a $1.4 million long-lived asset impairment charge that did not recur. Non‑GAAP net loss, which excludes non-cash stock-based compensation, non-cash expenses related to the change in the estimated fair value of the Securities Purchase Agreement put/call asset relating to the Company’s July 2025 private placement transaction and success payment liabilities, increased by $2.8 million to $40.6 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $37.8 million for the same period in 2025, primarily due to increased clinical trial activity and lower interest income. GAAP and Non-GAAP Operating Expenses Research and development (R&D) expenses were $39.5 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $34.9 million for the same period in 2025. The $4.7 million increase was primarily due to an $8.8 million increase in research activities, collaborations and outside services due to increased clinical trial activity, partially offset by a $4.2 million decrease in facilities and personnel expenses. Non‑GAAP R&D expenses, which exclude non-cash stock-based compensation, for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 were $37.4 million compared to $32.6 million for the same period in 2025. General and administrative (G&A) expenses were $9.6 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 compared to $9.8 million for the same period in 2025, primarily due to lower professional services expenses. Non‑GAAP G&A expenses, which exclude non-cash stock‑based compensation, for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 were $7.2 million compared to $7.1 million for the same period in 2025. A discussion of non-GAAP financial measures, including reconciliations of the most comparable U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) measures to non‑GAAP financial measures, is presented below under “Non-GAAP Financial Measures.” Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities as of June 30, 2026 were $228.0 million compared to $247.2 million as of December 31, 2025. Lyell believes that its current cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities balances will be sufficient to meet working capital and capital expenditure needs into the third quarter of 2027. About Lyell Immunopharma, Inc. Lyell is a late-stage clinical company advancing a pipeline of next-generation CAR T-cell therapies for patients with hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. To realize the potential of cell therapy for cancer, Lyell utilizes a suite of technologies to arm CAR T cells with enhancements needed to drive durable tumor cytotoxicity and achieve consistent and long-lasting clinical responses, including the ability to resist exhaustion, maintain qualities of durable stemness and function in the hostile tumor microenvironment. LyFE has commercial launch capability and is expected to have the capacity to manufacture more than 1,200 CAR T-cell doses per year. To learn more, please visit www.lyell.com. Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements expressed or implied in this press release include, but are not limited to, statements regarding: Lyell’s plans for its existing cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, and its expectation that its financial position and cash runway will be sufficient to meet working capital and capital expenditure needs into the third quarter of 2027; Lyell’s expectations around the progress of the PiNACLE and PiNACLE-H2H trials, including the expected timing for release of additional and pivotal data from the PiNACLE trial; the use of pivotal data from the PiNACLE trial to support a BLA submission to the FDA in 2027 and other expectations around enrollment and regulatory submissions; Lyell’s expectations around the progress of the U.S. Phase 1 trial for LYL273, including the expected timing for release of additional clinical data from this trial and an End-of-Phase 1 FDA meeting; the anticipated benefits of Orphan Drug, RMAT and Fast Track designations for ronde-cel and Fast Track designation for LYL273; the capability of LyFE to manufacture drug supply through potential commercial launch and its expected manufacturing capacity; the potential clinical benefits and therapeutic potential of Lyell’s product candidates; and other statements that are not historical fact. These statements are based on Lyell’s current plans, objectives, estimates, expectations and intentions, are not guarantees of future performance and inherently involve significant risks and uncertainties. Actual results and the timing of events could differ materially from those anticipated in such forward-looking statements as a result of these risks and uncertainties, which include, but are not limited to, risks and uncertainties related to: Lyell operates in a rapidly evolving industry and has a limited operating history; Lyell’s ability to successfully develop, manufacture and commercialize product candidates or its experiencing significant delays in doing so; Lyell’s dependence on the enrollment and retention of patients in its current and planned clinical trials for its product candidates; the potential for results of Lyell’s research, nonclinical studies or earlier clinical trials to not be predictive of future results; clinical development involving a lengthy and expensive process with uncertain outcomes; Lyell’s product candidates and technologies being based on novel technologies that are unproven and may not result in approvable or marketable products; Lyell facing substantial competition in a rapidly changing industry, which may result in others discovering, developing or commercializing products before or more successfully than it does; Lyell’s ability to obtain and maintain sufficient intellectual property protection for its product candidates; the complexity of manufacturing cellular therapies; Lyell’s ability to manufacture drug products for its clinical trials itself and any potential delays in further qualifying or in receiving regulatory approvals for any manufacturing facility or product candidates or in expanding its manufacturing capacity; Lyell’s reliance on third parties; implementation of Lyell’s strategic plans for its business and product candidates and Lyell’s realization of the expected benefits of such plans; the potential reduction of Lyell’s cash resources and fluctuations in Lyell’s operating results and financial condition as a result of Lyell’s milestone, royalty and success payment obligations; the sufficiency of Lyell’s capital resources and need for additional capital to achieve its goals; and other risks, including those described under the heading “Risk Factors” in Lyell’s Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, being filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission today. title: Seabridge Gold Files Second Quarter 2026 Report to Shareholders and Its Financial Statements and MD&A
body_text: Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - August 13, 2026) - Seabridge Gold (TSX: SEA) (NYSE: SA) announced today that it has filed its Report to Shareholders, Interim Financial Statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 on SEDAR+ . To review these documents on the Company website, please see https://www.seabridgegold.com/investors/financial-reports . Recent Highlights Extensive 2026 KSM field program to support the feasibility study advancing on schedule. US$100M credit facility enables KSM momentum to continue Engagement with preferred candidate for earn-in joint venture continues 2025 Sustainability Report published BC Supreme Court requires reconsideration of KSM Substantially Started Designation Spin-out of Courageous Lake project to shareholders completed Awarded Smithers Resource and Mining Excellence Award The Gold Market: Finding Stability Financial Results During the three-months ended June 30, 2026, Seabridge posted net income of $117.5 million ($1.08 per share) compared to a net profit of $12.3 million ($0.12 per share) for the same period in 2025. The increase in net income was largely driven by gains realized on the distribution of the Courageous Lake project. During the second quarter, Seabridge invested $32.5 million in mineral interests, property and equipment at its projects compared to $21.1 million invested in the second quarter of 2025. At June 30, 2026, net working capital was $53.6 million compared to $109.8 million at December 31, 2025. In July 2026, Seabridge arranged an unsecured, short-term loan agreement with a strategic investor for up to US$100 million. The Loan will be used to support the significant investments we are making in our summer season work programs at KSM. The loan is drawable at the Company's election in minimum calls of US$10 million each, has an interest rate of 7% compounded monthly, and is capitalized and matures on December 31, 2026. The Loan is repayable either in cash at any time or, in certain circumstances and subject to TSX approval, in common shares of Seabridge if outstanding at maturity, at the Company's option. The Loan includes customary conditions, representations, warranties and covenants. The Company intends to draw on the Loan, if required, to strengthen its consolidated liquidity position. No amounts are currently drawn on the Loan. About Seabridge Gold Seabridge Gold holds a 100% interest in several North American gold projects. Its principal assets are the KSM and Bronson Corridor projects in British Columbia's Golden Triangle. Additional projects include Snowstorm in Nevada's Getchell Gold Belt and the 3 Aces project in the Yukon. title: GRAIL Announces FDA Advisory Committee Meeting to Review Premarket Approval Application for the Galleri ® Multi-Cancer Early Detection Test
summary: MENLO PARK, Calif., Aug. 7, 2026 – GRAIL, Inc. (Nasdaq: GRAL), a healthcare company whose mission is to detect cancer early when it can be cured, today
body_text: August 7, 2026 MENLO PARK, Calif., Aug. 7, 2026 – GRAIL, Inc. (Nasdaq: GRAL), a healthcare company whose mission is to detect cancer early when it can be cured, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) Molecular and Clinical Genetics Panel of the Medical Devices Advisory Committee is scheduled to meet on Sept. 23, 2026 to review the Premarket Approval (PMA) application for the Galleri® multi-cancer early detection (MCED) blood test. The Galleri test is designed to detect cancer-specific methylation patterns shared by many types of cancer before symptoms appear, including cancers that do not have recommended screening today. When a cancer signal is detected, Galleri is designed to predict the cancer signal origin with high accuracy to help guide diagnostic evaluation. The test is intended to be used in addition to, and not as a replacement for, guideline-recommended screenings. “Today, the status quo in cancer screening is simply unacceptable. Many cancers are detected too late, after symptoms appear and the disease is too advanced for effective or curative-intent treatments. In fact, 70-80% of cancer deaths occur due to cancers we are not screening for at all. GRAIL has pioneered a breakthrough technology, the Galleri test, designed to transform cancer screening by detecting more cancers before symptoms appear, including many of the deadly cancers that lack recommended screenings today. The Galleri technology is unique in how it is designed to examine the methylome using proprietary technology and artificial intelligence. We have generated extensive data in multiple studies to evaluate the impact of adding Galleri to standard of care screening with positive results showing evidence of increases in screen detected cancers, a low false positive rate and high signal origin prediction accuracy. Adding Galleri to recommended screening could result in a more effective and efficient cancer screening program in the U.S.,” said Josh Ofman, MD, MSHS, CEO at GRAIL. “Galleri is the only MCED test supported by large interventional and randomized, controlled studies in intended use populations. We appreciate the FDA’s leadership in advancing the review of the first premarket approval application for an MCED, and we look forward to discussing Galleri’s clinical data and the opportunity for multi-cancer early detection to address a significant unmet public health need, with the Advisory Committee.” GRAIL submitted its PMA application for Galleri to the FDA on Jan. 29, 2026. The FDA designated Galleri as a Breakthrough Device in 2018. The PMA submission is focused on the test performance and safety results from 25,490 consented participants with one year of follow up in the US-based PATHFINDER 2 study as well as data from over 70,000 participants from the intervention arm of the prevalent screening round (first year) of the NHS-Galleri trial, the largest and only randomized, controlled trial of an MCED test in an intended use population. The submission is also supported by an analysis to compare performance of the version of Galleri used in the PATHFINDER 2 study and the NHS-Galleri trial to the updated PMA version that has been submitted to the FDA for premarket approval. About GRAIL GRAIL is a healthcare company whose mission is to detect cancer early, when it can be cured. GRAIL is focused on alleviating the global burden of cancer by using the power of next-generation sequencing, population-scale clinical studies, and state-of-the-art machine learning, software, and automation to detect and identify multiple deadly cancer types in earlier stages. GRAIL’s targeted methylation-based platform can support the continuum of care for screening and precision oncology. GRAIL is headquartered in Menlo Park, Calif. with locations in Washington, D.C., North Carolina, and the United Kingdom. For more information, visit grail.com . title: How to Reduce Cart Abandonment Across Stages of the Full Buyer Journey
summary: Zoko is an all-in-one system that leverages the WhatsApp API to help you do business, on WhatsApp. Go beyond chatting - reach customers, enable product discovery, collect payments, get feedback - all on WhatsApp.
body_text: Every abandoned cart hurts more when you know the shopper was already interested. They saw the product, checked the price, picked a variant, and still left. For Shopify merchants, that drop-off often points to several small frictions working together. Maybe shipping costs appeared too late. Maybe the COD terms felt unclear. Possibly the buyer had a sizing question, a delivery concern, or a payment issue and found no quick answer. Baymard Institute’s research puts the average cart abandonment rate at 70.22% , indicating this is a common revenue leak rather than an edge case. That's why we've compiled this guide to help you reduce cart abandonment by understanding what makes shoppers pause before they pay. You will learn how to reduce shopping cart abandonment across product pages, pricing, delivery details, checkout steps, payment choices, and follow-up messages. ‍ In a Nutshell To reduce cart abandonment, you must remove buyer doubts before checkout, make payment easier, and recover shoppers through useful follow-ups. Cart abandonment reveals where purchase intent breaks down, often due to unclear pricing, delivery concerns, low trust, or checkout friction. Before checkout, clearly show shipping fees, taxes, COD availability, discount terms, delivery dates, return rules, and stock status. On product pages, answer purchase-blocking questions with size guides, FAQs, reviews, return links, and quick support options. During checkout, offer guest checkout, reduce form fields, enable autofill, show order summaries, and support secure payment modes, including UPI, wallets, cards, and COD. After abandonment, send timely, personalized cart reminders with the product name, cart link, price, offer terms, and a clear next step. WhatsApp-based recovery can help Shopify stores answer questions on sizing, delivery, COD, returns, and payment before intent fades. ‍ What Cart Abandonment Really Means for Your Shopify Store Cart abandonment happens when a shopper adds products to their online cart but leaves before completing the purchase. It can happen early in checkout, while entering payment details, or even just before placing the order. For Shopify merchants like you, it shows a gap between purchase intent and checkout completion. The shopper liked the product enough to add it to the cart, but something stopped them from buying. ‍ How to Calculate It: Use this formula to calculate your cart abandonment rate: Cart Abandonment Rate = [1 − Completed Purchases ÷ Carts Created] × 100 Example: If your Shopify store created 1,000 carts in a week and received 300 completed purchases, your cart abandonment rate would be: [1 − (300 ÷ 1,000)] × 100 = 70% ‍ Why Ready-to-Buy Shoppers Leave Before Payment: Common Must-Know Reasons Shoppers usually abandon carts when something breaks their confidence before payment. Most drop-offs come from a mix of cost, trust, checkout, delivery, and payment friction. Common reasons include: Unexpected costs: Shoppers may rethink the order when shipping fees, taxes, or extra charges appear late in checkout. Forced account creation: Many buyers do not want to create an account before ordering. Forter’s Trust Premium Report says 23% of surveyed consumers have abandoned carts because account creation was required. Complicated checkout forms: Too many fields slow users down and make the order feel harder. Limited payment options: Customers expect payment methods that match their habits (e.g., UPI, digital wallets, cards, or COD). Payment issues: A cluttered payment page or a failed payment attempt can stop a ready buyer. Lack of trust: Shoppers hesitate when return policies, delivery timelines, payment safety, or brand details feel unclear. Technical errors and slow pages: Slow load times, crashes, or cart errors can make shoppers leave immediately and reduce store trust. Casual browsing: Some shoppers add products only to compare prices or save items for later. Also Read: Winning Back Customers: Zoko's Abandoned Cart Recovery Magic ‍ How to Reduce Cart Abandonment Across the Buying Journey Reducing cart abandonment is not about fixing one checkout button. It involves removing doubts before checkout, reducing friction during checkout, and following up after shoppers leave. For you, each stage matters because buyers can drop off even after showing very clear purchase intent. ‍ Before Checkout: Remove Doubt Before the Shopper Reaches Payment Before checkout, your goal is to make shoppers feel clear, confident, and ready to buy. Many carts are abandoned because the buyer does not know the final cost, delivery date, return rules, or product details early enough. ‍ Quick Checklist for Shopify Merchants Shopper concern What to fix “What will I actually pay?” Show shipping fees, taxes, COD charges, and discount terms early. “Will this product work for me?” Add size guides, product FAQs, reviews, and return policy links. “When will this arrive?” Display estimated delivery dates before checkout. “Is this still available?” Show real-time stock updates and low-stock indicators. “Can I shop easily on mobile?” Use fast pages, readable text, and easy-to-tap CTAs. To reduce abandonment before checkout, consider the following: Show full costs early: Display delivery charges, taxes, coupon terms, and COD availability before the cart page. Use shipping calculators or flat-rate shipping where possible. Answer buying questions on product pages: Add FAQs, return details, delivery estimates, stock availability, reviews, and clear variant information. For example, a Shopify fashion store can place a size guide and exchange policy near “Add to Cart.” Keep mobile browsing simple: Use clear menus, short product paths, fast-loading pages, and visible buttons like “Add to Cart” and “Proceed to Checkout.” Use product recommendations carefully: Suggest relevant products based on browsing behavior, but avoid showing too many choices. Support repeat purchases: For subscription products like pet food or skincare, add quick-reorder options so repeat buyers don't have to start from scratch. Add real-time help before shoppers leave: Use AI chatbots or WhatsApp support prompts to answer questions about products, delivery, returns, or payments. A synced WhatsApp Catalog can also help shoppers browse inside WhatsApp. ‍ During Checkout: Make the Final Step Fast, Clear, and Trustworthy During checkout, shoppers want speed and certainty. They need to confirm what they are buying, how much they will pay, when it will arrive, and whether the payment is safe. ‍ Check out the Friction Checklist for Shopify Merchants Checkout concern What to fix “Why is this taking so long?” Shorten checkout steps and reduce the number of form fields. Use "autofill" for returning customers. “Why do I need to create an account?” Offer guest checkout for first-time shoppers. “Can I pay my way?” Add cards, UPI, wallets, prepaid options, BNPL, and COD where relevant. “Is this payment safe?” Show SSL cues, secure payment badges, and trusted payment icons. “What exactly am I paying for?” Show item details, quantity, taxes, shipping, discounts, and final total. “Will my COD order be handled properly?” Confirm address, COD terms, delivery status, and tracking clearly. To reduce shopping cart abandonment during checkout: Shorten the checkout flow: Keep checkout between three to five clear steps, or use a single-page checkout where possible. Combine shipping, billing, and payment details without clutter. Add a progress indicator for clarity. Offer guest checkout: Many first-time buyers do not want to create an account before ordering. Let them buy first, then invite them to create an account after payment. Minimize form fields: Ask only for details needed to complete the order, such as name, address, contact number, and payment information. Use autofill for returning customers: Returning shoppers should not re-enter the same address or payment details. Saved information can make repeat buying faster. Show a clear order summary: Display product name, quantity, price, discount, shipping fee, taxes, and final total before payment to remove last-minute confusion. Offer preferred payment methods: Include secure payment options such as cards, UPI, digital wallets, BNPL, prepaid options, and COD where relevant. Build trust before payment: Show secure payment badges, SSL certifications, PCI DSS compliance, recognized payment icons, reviews, ratings, and support contact details near checkout. Reduce COD uncertainty: COD-heavy stores should clearly confirm order details, delivery address, and tracking information. ‍ After Exit: Recover Shoppers Without Sounding Pushy Some shoppers will still leave. They may get distracted, compare prices, wait for payday, or need one more reason to trust the purchase. After their exits, your goal is to bring them back. ‍ Abandoned Cart Recovery Checklist for Shopify Merchants Recovery concern What to fix “The shopper left. What now?” Send a timely cart reminder through email, SMS, or WhatsApp. “Will a discount bring them back?” Use offers only when helpful, not as the only recovery tactic. “What should the message include?” Add product name, cart link, price, offer terms, and a clear CTA. “How do we avoid sounding pushy?” Keep the sequence short and easy to opt out of. “Can ads bring them back?” Use retargeting ads for products viewed or abandoned. “What can we learn from exits?” Review drop-off data, feedback, messages, and A/B test results. Use these recovery methods: Send timely cart reminders: Follow up on abandoned carts with a clear, personalized reminder. Use email, SMS, WhatsApp, or retargeting based on customers’ preferred and opted-in channels. Be specific about the message: Mention the product name, cart link, price, subject line, and any active offer. Use WhatsApp for fast recovery: WhatsApp reminders can help when shoppers need quick answers. Include a direct CTA such as “Resume My Order” or “Complete Checkout.” Did you know? WhatsApp's 2026 State of Business Messaging report found that 73.3% of consumers across 22 markets prefer messaging to communicate with businesses. That supports the use of WhatsApp via platforms like Zoko for abandoned cart reminders, support-led recovery, and quick answers. Do not rely only on discounts: Some shoppers need answers more than coupons. Offer help with size, delivery, COD, return policy, or payment doubts. Use urgency carefully: Limited-time discounts, free shipping windows, or low-stock alerts can encourage action. Keep the message honest and avoid false pressure. Run retargeting ads: Retargeting can remind shoppers of products they viewed or abandoned while they browse elsewhere, helping maintain brand recall. Use exit-intent offers: If shoppers move to leave, show a simple and easy-to-close last-minute reminder, discount, or support prompt. Send post-purchase follow-ups: After purchase, send a thank you note, confirmation details, shipping timelines, tracking information, and support options. Study behavior and feedback: Review drop-off points, customer messages, surveys, reviews, and A/B test results. Test checkout layouts, CTA text, button placement, and reminder messages. Also Read: Step-by-Step Guide to Recovering Abandoned Carts on WhatsApp ‍ How Zoko Helps You Move Cart Recovery Into WhatsApp Without Turning It Into a Hard Sell ‍ Many shoppers abandon their carts because they still have genuine questions about delivery, payment, COD, sizing, returns, or product fit. For Shopify merchants, WhatsApp can be a practical recovery channel because customers already use it to ask quick buying questions. Instead of sending only a discount, a WhatsApp-first recovery flow can help shoppers complete the decision they already started. ‍ Where Zoko Fits Into Cart Recovery Zoko helps you bring cart recovery into WhatsApp, where the conversation can continue naturally after a shopper leaves the store. The goal is not to send more messages. It is to send more useful messages at the right time. Relevant features include: Abandoned checkout recovery with FlowHippo Flows: You can set up automated reminders when shoppers leave items behind. These reminders can include the product, cart link, and a clear next step. COD confirmation flows: For COD-heavy stores, Zoko can help confirm orders , addresses, and buyer intent before fulfillment, reducing manual follow-up. AI chatbot support : A chatbot can answer common questions about delivery times, size concerns, payment, return rules, and order status. WhatsApp Catalog: Useful before abandonment, a synced WhatsApp Catalog lets shoppers browse products, ask questions, and move closer to purchase within WhatsApp. Shopify and Shiprocket-connected workflows: Shopify maintains the cart and order context, while Shiprocket support helps with COD and logistics clarity. And this approach works in real cart recovery scenarios. For instance, Zoko helped 1 Hair Stop recover $57K from 564 abandoned carts in 90 days through WhatsApp-based abandoned cart recovery. ‍ Conclusion Learning how to reduce cart abandonment starts with seeing each drop-off as a signal, not a lost cause. When shoppers leave, they are usually reacting to unclear costs, slow checkout, limited payment choices, weak trust signals, or unanswered questions. Fixing these points helps you protect paid traffic, improve buyer confidence, and move more interested shoppers toward completed orders. Once those basics are clearer, the next step is staying available when shoppers still need help. That is where Zoko fits naturally for Shopify merchants. It lets you use WhatsApp to answer questions, send abandoned checkout reminders, showcase products through Catalog, and clarify COD confirmations through Shiprocket-linked workflows. Book a demo to explore how Zoko helps you realize that in practice and evaluate the recovery workflows that make the most sense for your store. ‍ FAQs ‍ 1. What should we check first when cart abandonment suddenly increases? Start by checking changes in final pricing, shipping charges, payment success, page speed, and checkout errors. A sudden rise often means shoppers are facing a new friction point, not simply losing interest. Also review recent customer messages, failed payment data, and abandoned checkout reports to spot repeated issues faster. ‍ 2. Can we reduce cart abandonment without offering discounts? Yes, discounts are not the only way to recover carts. Many shoppers leave because they need clearer costs, faster answers, preferred payment options, or delivery confidence. If you want to reduce cart abandonment without cutting margins, start with cost clarity, guest checkout, trust signals, and real-time support. ‍ 3. How can we know if abandonment is caused by pricing or checkout friction? Compare where shoppers leave. If many leave after viewing the final total, pricing or delivery costs may be the issue. If they leave after entering checkout, form length, account creation, payment concerns, or technical errors may be stronger causes. ‍ 4. Should we treat all abandoned carts the same way? No. A high-value cart, a repeat-customer cart, and a first-time-visitor cart require different follow-ups. Repeat buyers may need a quick cart link, while first-time shoppers may need return details, delivery clarity, or support. This makes segmentation useful for planning how to reduce cart abandonment without sending generic reminders.

title: Investing in a bond ETF (bond ETFs)
summary: Bond ETFs: how they work, risk profile, PEA eligibility and 2026 taxation. Benefits, limits and practical tips for choosing the right tracker.
body_text: Updated on 3 August 2026 A bond ETF is an exchange-traded index fund that replicates a basket of dozens to hundreds of government or corporate bonds, in a single order. Less risky than equities but more dynamic than a euro fund, it gives low-cost access, with deep liquidity, to a market long reserved for institutional investors. Key takeaways Its risk profile sits between the euro fund and equities, with management fees of around 0.2% a year. Its performance depends on the composition of the basket (governments, corporates, high yield) and on the direction of interest rates. No conventional bond ETF is eligible for the PEA (a French tax-advantaged equity savings account): only an equivalent euro money-market fund is available there today. In a securities account, capital gains and coupons are subject to the flat tax (PFU) of 31.4% in 2026. Unlike a conventional bond, a bond ETF trades continuously like a share, which makes entering and exiting the bond market easier. What is a bond ETF? A bond ETF is an index fund that replicates a basket of government or corporate bonds, listed and tradable on an exchange like a share. Here is how it differs from other bond vehicles. What is a bond? A bond is a debt security representing a loan taken out by a company or a government. Bondholders are paid through the interest generated by that debt. In principle, retail investors reach this type of market product through collective investment schemes (OPCVM, the French UCITS framework), via a securities account, life insurance or a PEA. They fall into 4 broad categories depending on their composition: bond, diversified, equity and money-market OPCVM. Within these OPCVM, bonds can take 3 forms: bond SICAV (Société d’investissement à capital variable, an open-ended investment company), which let you become a shareholder in the fund by buying units the FCP (Fonds Commun de Placement, a French mutual fund), which makes you a co-owner of the bonds and bond ETFs , which are index funds made up of bonds traded on an exchange. They let you invest on the stock market in dozens, even hundreds of securities in a single order. Bring your whole net worth together PEA, savings accounts, cryptocurrencies, shares, property, bank accounts. Discover Finary How does a bond ETF work? An ETF (Exchange-Traded Fund) is a fund that copies the composition and the performance of a reference index. Its aim is therefore not to beat the index, but to track it as closely as possible . For example, a CAC 40 ETF seeks to reproduce the performance of the CAC 40, letting you invest in one go in every company in that index. The same goes for a World ETF , which replicates the MSCI World, the index covering the 1,600 largest companies worldwide. What is the risk profile of a bond ETF? Bonds are riskier than euro funds , but less risky than equities. A bond ETF therefore mainly suits investors who traditionally choose the equity market or who have a moderate risk profile. What determines the risk profile is the composition of the bond ETF . Emerging-market government debt, treasury bills and corporate bonds do not move in the same way and do not trade on the same markets. So take care when choosing your tracker, and analyse its basket closely. Depending on your risk profile, some trackers cover floating-rate bonds to anticipate possible interest-rate rises, such as the Amundi Floating Rate Euro Corporate 1-3 UCITS ETF , and others are ethical ETFs such as the Amundi Global Aggregate Green Bond UCITS ETF (formerly Lyxor Green Bond) or the iShares € Green Bond UCITS ETF . Finally, a global bond ETF lets you dilute concentration risk. The Amundi Core Global Aggregate Bond UCITS ETF (formerly Amundi Index Barclays Global Agg 500M) holds more than 11,500 securities. Good to know : some mixed bond ETFs are not made up of 100% bonds : they often combine a majority of bonds with a share of equities and alternative assets. That makes them more dynamic , but they do not suit the same investor profile. Always check that the fund has a UCITS prospectus before investing in it from France. What are the advantages of a bond ETF? Passive management, access to the bond market and diversification: a bond ETF has plenty going for it. Passive management, a lower-cost solution The main appeal of ETFs, bond or otherwise, lies in their passive management . They give you access to hundreds of securities in a single order and require few switches. Fees are generally low, around 0.2% on average (0.10% to 0.25% across the bond ETFs checked). This passive management lets you build a diversified wealth management strategy. A bond ETF gives you low-cost access to a large number of bonds through a flexible instrument: you buy and sell bond ETFs in real time. That intraday liquidity can help you adjust your exposure when the market moves. Spot your hidden fees Finary users save an average of €44,077 on their hidden fees Discover Finary Easier access to bonds A bond ETF lets investors reach a market that can be hard to access for retail investors. Primary-market bonds are not listed on an exchange and their prices are negotiated over the counter, which makes transactions relatively opaque. Trackers, by contrast, offer transparent prices and trade throughout the day, even when the bonds they hold do not. Access to bonds is smoother as a result. The secondary market for ETFs also offers investors a further source of liquidity. Far from negligible, it can let you trade securities at a lower amount than on the primary market , especially on high-volume bond ETFs. Simpler portfolio diversification Bond ETFs bring welcome variety to your asset portfolio. Although appreciably riskier than euro funds, bonds have the advantage of being more dynamic while remaining uncorrelated with equities . This type of vehicle gives you a large number of diversified assets within the same class with little effort and, above all, at a much lower price than building the basket yourself. Depending on your profile and your objectives, a bond ETF can find a place in a diversified portfolio, but it has to be chosen carefully to deliver the expected effect. Apps such as Finary let you track the performance of your bond ETFs in one place, alongside the rest of your portfolio, across every broker. Good to know : more and more investors are looking at bond ETFs, and these products have changed a great deal to match demand and needs. The ESG approach features increasingly often, and asset managers extend their ranges every year . Compare the trackers available to work out which one matches your performance and risk objectives . Is a bond ETF eligible for the PEA? ETFs invested in government or corporate bonds are, as a rule, not eligible for the PEA . The only historical "bond" route in, the Lyxor PEA Oblig Euro UCITS ETF (ISIN FR0013346681), has changed nature: since October 2024 it has been renamed Amundi PEA Euro Court Terme UCITS ETF and no longer replicates euro-zone government debt but the €STR rate (the overnight interbank rate). It is now closer to a money-market ETF than to a true bond ETF. In practice, for a PEA investor, this fund mainly serves to park cash temporarily at a yield close to euro-zone short-term rates, with management fees of 0.25% a year. For conventional bond exposure, a securities account or life insurance is a better route, as both offer a far wider choice of bond ETFs. The best PEA ETFs remain equity ETFs. The Finary life insurance simulator estimates the impact of a withdrawal for your situation. Good to know : a bond ETF opens the door to a market investors often overlook, for lack of access and understanding. In an uncertain economy, this tracker brings volatility that is generally lower than equities , particularly with Western government bonds. Investors used to equity exposure can therefore turn to bond ETFs to diversify their portfolio with moderate-risk assets and gain broader diversification. High-yield bond ETFs carry a higher default risk and are aimed at experienced investors. Frequently asked questions Which are the best bond ETFs? Amundi offers a wide range of bond ETFs: the Lyxor brand was folded into Amundi between 2021 and 2023 after the acquisition. No conventional bond tracker is eligible for the PEA: the only PEA-compatible ETF, the Amundi PEA Euro Court Terme, now replicates a money-market index rather than government debt. Among the bond ETFs frequently cited, in no order and with no recommendation: iShares € Govt Bond 7-10yr UCITS ETF, Amundi Index Euro Corporate SRI UCITS ETF, Amundi Core Global Government Bond UCITS ETF and Amundi Euro High Yield Bond ESG UCITS ETF. Can you invest in a bond ETF through a PEA? Not really any more: the only PEA-compatible fund with a bond component, the Amundi PEA Euro Court Terme UCITS ETF (formerly Lyxor PEA Oblig Euro), changed nature in October 2024. It now replicates the overnight €STR rate rather than a basket of government bonds: it mainly serves to park cash, not to gain bond exposure. What are the different types of bonds? Unlike shares, bonds are a debt security, not an ownership title. They can be government, corporate, association or treasury bills, and so on. This debt can carry a fixed or a floating rate. Bond ETFs track indices made up of one or several types of bonds, in one or several geographies. A high-yield bond ETF is a tracker that follows indices such as the Bloomberg Fixed Income Indices or the ICE BofA Indices (formerly the Bloomberg Barclays and Bank of America Merrill Lynch indices, renamed in 2021 and 2017 respectively). They carry additional default risk compared with conventional bond ETFs. How is a bond ETF taxed? In a securities account, capital gains and coupons fall under the flat tax (PFU). According to the French tax authority (impots.gouv.fr), gains realised since 01/01/2018 are subject to this levy, whose overall rate is 31.4% (12.8% for income tax and 18.6% for social levies). Held via life insurance, a bond ETF benefits from reduced taxation after 8 years. In a PEA, the wrapper is exempt from income tax after 5 years, excluding social levies. Should you choose an accumulating or a distributing bond ETF? An accumulating ETF automatically reinvests the coupons, which compounds returns and simplifies management. A distributing ETF pays you the interest at regular intervals, useful for generating income. The choice depends on your objective: growing your capital or drawing an income. What effect does a rate rise have on a bond ETF? When interest rates rise, the value of bonds already issued falls, and the ETF holding them declines in the short term. The longer the maturity (duration) of the bonds, the stronger this effect. Conversely, newly issued bonds then offer higher coupons, which supports future returns. title: Payroll Budgeting in Nigeria: How Businesses Can Plan Salary Costs and Avoid Cash Flow Gaps
summary: Finance Payroll Budgeting in Nigeria: How Businesses Can Plan Salary Costs and Avoid Cash Flow Gaps Oluwakemi Adesina August 8, 2026 Payroll budgeting in Nigeria is a step to protecting your cash flow. It is one of your biggest recurring expenses. It stays the same whether sales are up or down, or a client pays late. Skipping payroll planning means salaries are not properly planned for. And when there is growth, like a new hire joining mid-quarter, bonus week, or even remittance season, cash probably runs short. It affects the business operations. The team scrambles to move money rather than run the business. Here is how to build a payroll budget that protects your cash flow. Payroll Processing and Budgeting: The Difference A payroll budget forecasts what you will spend on employee compensation each quarter or year. Payroll processing is paying your team for work already done. It happens at month-end. Payroll budgeting comes first. It asks: What can the business really afford to spend on our workforce over the next year? A business that relies solely on processing experiences headcount growth, statutory updates, and annual bonuses as a series of stressful financial shocks. Conversely, a business that practices proactive workforce budgeting handles these shifts smoothly. The funds are already planned. To make this work, finance and HR teams must break down their organizational silos. HR tracks hiring pipelines, promotions, and exit dates, while finance tracks cash runways and revenue targets. The 6 Layers of a Nigerian Payroll Budget An accurate payroll budget requires looking beyond basic salaries. Most businesses face cash flow gaps because they under-forecast, ignoring hidden variables that increase the total cost of employment. According to international standards, comprehensive salary planning must include all fair compensation parameters, including allowances and statutory protections. To build an airtight forecast, you must implement strict salary cost planning across all six layers of the labor stack: Basic Salaries: This is your baseline. It represents the fixed, non-negotiable monthly cost of your current staff. Contractual Allowances: Under Nigerian labor structures, base pay is often split. You must account for recurring contractual allowances like housing, transport, and utilities specified in employment contracts. Guidelines from the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment outline how these wage components interact with local regulations. Variable Compensations: If your business pays a 13th-month salary, performance bonuses, or sales commissions, these must be forecasted based on performance tiers. Overtime Pay: If you run logistics, hospitality, manufacturing, or retail, overtime matters. Check last year’s data for peak months, such as December. Budget more for overtime in those periods. Statutory Obligations: Compliance costs rise automatically as your team grows. In Nigeria, your budget must factor in pension contributions, the Industrial Training Fund (ITF), and NSITF employee compensation insurance. Skipping these calculations leaves a massive compliance gap in your annual financial layout. Perks and Medical Benefits: Add up the full cost of Group Life Insurance, HMO premiums, staff training, and leave allowances. Step-by-Step Employee Cost Budgeting for Your Business You do not need complex models to build a real forecast. Follow these steps to plan your year: Step 1: Set your baseline. Pull payroll data from the last three months. Add up basic pay, allowances, and statutory costs. This is your current run-rate. Step 2: Layer the Hiring Timeline. Review your company’s growth plans. If HR plans to bring on a new manager in Q3, do not just add their salary to the annual total. Map the full cost stack to start precisely in July. Step 3: Add adjustments. Include promotions, cost-of-living increases, or market corrections. Update your baseline for the exact months these changes start. Step 4: Add Statutory Calculations. Calculate your pension, ITF, and NSITF obligations based on your projected headcount growth, ensuring you use the correct local compliance percentages. Step 5: Add a buffer You cannot predict sudden market changes or emergency hires. Always add a 5%-10% buffer to your monthly allocation to cover unexpected employee expenses. Data security is a key part of administrative safety. When handling financial and personal details during payroll mapping, businesses must ensure security and comply with the Regulations. Why Is Payroll Budgeting Nigeria Critical for Cash Flow? The primary objective of salary budgeting in Nigeria is to protect your liquid cash reserves before payday. A reliable payroll forecasting strategy gives business leaders a clear, three-month runway. When you can see exactly where statutory payments, new hire onboarding, and bonus periods intersect, you gain the foresight to manage cash reserves effectively. You can confidently adjust project timelines, manage vendor payments, or hold back discretionary spending before a crunch happens. Delayed salaries quickly erode employee trust. In the market today, maintaining a reputation for paying on time, every time, is your strongest tool for talent retention. 3 Payroll Budgeting Mistakes Nigerian Businesses Should Avoid The “Set and Forget” Trap A budget is a living document. A plan created in January becomes obsolete by April if your team scales faster than expected or if market realities force salary adjustments. Review the forecast quarterly to keep calculations aligned with reality. 2. Cash Flow Timing Blindspots Your annual calculations might be accurate, but poor timing can still break your business. If annual performance bonuses, insurance renewals, and tax remittances all fall in the same month, you will hit a cash crunch. High payroll expenses in Nigeria must be balanced against real-time cash inflows. 3. Siloed Planning When HR sets hiring targets without cross-checking the finance team’s cash runway, capital strain follows. Finance should never discover a payroll increase on disbursement day. Frequently Asked Questions What is payroll budgeting? It is the strategic practice of forecasting every naira your business will spend on salaries, allowances, statutory remittances, and bonuses over an upcoming quarter or year. A comprehensive budget must include basic salaries, housing and transport allowances, statutory contributions (Pension, ITF, NSITF), seasonal bonuses, overtime estimates, and staff perks like HMO premiums.
