title: The best AI product photography tools: 6 compared for 2026
summary: Six AI product photography tools compared on features and real 2026 pricing, so you can match one to your store.
body_text: TL;DR The best AI product photography tool in 2026 depends on what you sell and how much you produce. There is no universal winner, so we compared six tools across the jobs ecommerce teams actually run: cutouts, lifestyle scenes, on-model shots and video. Our three headline picks: Claid AI is best for fidelity-critical catalogs, because its AI keeps logos, labels and shape intact while generating scenes and on-model shots at volume. Presti is best for brand and content teams producing at scale, because you brief it in plain language and it generates on-brand images and video across a whole catalog. Photoroom is best for solo founders and small sellers, because it turns a phone photo into a clean, listing-ready image on mobile from $9.99/month. The tables below cover all six tools we compared: Claid AI, Presti, Photoroom, Flair AI, Mokker AI and Rewarx Studio. Why this comparison exists In ecommerce, the image is the product. Shoppers can't hold what you sell, so the photo does the selling. UX research from the Baymard Institute found that the first thing 56% of shoppers do on a product page is look at the images, before the title or the description. A widely cited Shopify figure adds that products with professional photos convert around 33% higher than those with low-quality ones. Little wonder that, according to the World Federation of Advertisers, 78% of brands now use AI-generated or AI-enhanced content in marketing, with product images the single most common use at 87%. Traditional shoots still produce beautiful work, but the economics are hard at catalog scale. Across 2026 pricing guides, a basic white-background image runs about $25 to $75, styled lifestyle shots $100 to $500 or more, and a full-day studio session well into the thousands. AI product photography software brings the per-image cost down to a few dollars or less, which is why most growing brands now run a hybrid: AI for volume, real photography for the flagship few. We build in this category, so we follow these tools closely. This guide is the most complete breakdown we could produce: how we compared them, a quick comparison, a deep dive per tool, a full feature matrix, guidance by industry, and an expanded FAQ. We include our own product, Presti, and hold it to exactly the same standard as the rest, strengths and weaknesses alike. How we compared these tools We wanted a comparison you can trust, so we set a few ground rules. Official sources for every fact. Every price and feature claim was checked on the vendor's own pages on August 10, 2026. Anything we could not confirm on an official source is marked [verify] rather than repeated from a secondhand roundup. Compared across four jobs. We looked at each tool through the four jobs a real catalog needs, clean cutouts, lifestyle scenes, on-model output and video, rather than a single hero image, so the comparison reflects day-to-day ecommerce work. Grounded in category experience. We build in this space, so our read on each tool's strengths and limits draws on working in AI product imagery alongside each vendor's documentation and sample output. Our own bias, stated. Presti is our product. We flag that openly and apply the same criteria and the same "where it falls short" section to it as to every competitor. The state of AI product photography in 2026 Three shifts define the category this year, and they shape which tools are safe bets. Consolidation has started. soona acquired Mokker (the generative-AI studio founded in 2019 as Zerolens) back in 2024, and Mokker still runs standalone while also powering soona's own tools. It is a sign the space is maturing from single features into platforms. Serious money backs the leaders. Photoroom counts Y Combinator and AI pioneer Yann LeCun among its backers, and Presti raised a $3.5M seed from Partech and Y Combinator, so the tools you adopt now are likely to keep shipping and supporting you. Adoption is mainstream, and buyers notice. According to the World Federation of Advertisers, 78% of brands now use AI-generated or AI-enhanced content in marketing, and product images are the single most common use at 87%. That matters because images do the selling: Baymard Institute found the first thing 56% of shoppers do on a product page is look at the images. The open question is no longer whether to use AI, but how to use it well. Quick comparison Prices in USD, monthly billing unless noted, from each vendor's pricing page on August 10 , 2026. They vary by region, promotion and app store, so confirm at checkout. Tool Best for Standout features Starting price Free option Claid AI Fidelity-critical catalogs and fashion on-model Fidelity-focused AI, 4K on top tier, AI fashion models, API Essential from $15/mo Free trial, 50 credits Presti Brand and content teams producing at scale Brief-driven agent, multi-model, image and video, on-model, up to 8K $49/mo (500 credits) Yes, 60 credits/mo Photoroom Solo founders, small Shopify and marketplace sellers Mobile-first editing, batch, Shopify publishing, Virtual Model $9.99/mo (monthly) Yes, watermarked Flair AI Marketers and agencies wanting creative control Drag-and-drop scene canvas, 3D props, fashion models, ad creatives $10/mo (Pro) Yes, limited Mokker AI Sellers needing fast studio/white-background shots One-click studio scenes, 100+ templates, batch, category-aware AI $13/mo (Starter) Yes, 20 photos Rewarx Studio Catalog teams wanting a full studio suite by industry On-model, ghost mannequin, try-on, 4K, product page builder ~$11/mo (Starter, €9.90) Free trial What 150 product images a month actually costs Headline prices only mean something once you translate them into a real monthly bill. Below is what it costs to generate about 150 product images a month, no video, on each tool's cheapest plan that covers that volume, on standard monthly billing (not discounted annual plans, since most people start month to month). Euro-based plans are converted at about $1.08 per euro as of August 2026. Tool Cheapest monthly plan covering ~150 images Monthly cost Notes Photoroom Pro (up to 1,600 AI image generations) $9.99 Comfortably covers 150; one of the lowest per-image costs at scale Mokker AI Team (500 photos) $29 Starter ($13) may also cover 150, but its photo cap isn't published Claid AI Pro (~2,000 credits) $49 150 images fit inside the monthly credit pool Presti Pro (500 credits ≈ 166 images) $49 1 image = 3 credits; covers 150 with headroom, video also available Flair AI Scale Tier 1 (150 images) $55 Pro+ ($35) caps at 80 images, so 150 needs the Scale tier Rewarx Studio Growth (200 credits, 1 credit = 1 standard image) ~$59 (€54.90) Starter (100 credits) sits below 150; billed in EUR At this volume, Photoroom and Mokker AI are the cheapest routes, for cutout-led and studio-style work respectively. Claid AI, Presti, Flair AI and Rewarx cluster in the roughly $40 to $60 range, which is broadly what you pay for on-model output, video or higher fidelity. The economics shift again past ~150 images a month: Flair moves to higher Scale tiers and Presti to add-on credits or a custom plan, so re-check the math at your real volume. These are generation prices only; expiring credits, per-session batch caps and separately billed APIs still move the final number, which is why we say read the pricing page twice. Claid AI: product fidelity for catalogs and fashion What it is. Claid AI is a product photography AI suite built by the team behind the upscaling tool Let's Enhance, and that heritage shows in cutout and resolution quality. Its core, AI Photoshoot, turns a single product photo into clean catalog shots and lifestyle scenes, and its AI Fashion Models place a garment on an AI-generated model. It also handles background removal, upscaling, light and color correction, outpainting and image-to-video, and its AI is tuned to preserve logos, branding and shape, which is why marketplaces and catalog teams reach for it. Claid lists Rappi, Zepto and Kasta among its customers. Pricing. Credit-based, with two separate systems for web and API. A free trial includes 50 credits. Paid tiers are Essential (from about $15/month), Pro ($49/month) and a custom Business plan. All paid plans include 2K output; 4K is on the top tier. Credits do not roll over. Best for: ecommerce and marketplace teams where a distorted logo or the wrong product shape is unacceptable, and apparel brands that need on-model shots without a studio. Where it falls short: the credit model gets expensive at very high volume, and the split web/API pricing makes forecasting harder. Creative mode can occasionally shift a product's angle, so hero shots may need a review pass, and low-resolution inputs limit results. Presti: a brief-driven agent for image and video at scale What it is. Presti (operated by Teker AI SAS, Paris) began in the furniture world and has grown into a broader ecommerce tool that behaves like a production agent rather than a single-image editor. You describe what you need and attach what you have; it generates images and video, routing each task to one of several third-party generative models under the hood, a multi-model approach its own terms confirm (naming providers such as Kling AI for video). It generates on-model shots with AI models, exports up to 8K via upscaling, and offers an API for automation. The workflow is built to keep a look consistent across many products. Presti says it is used by 400+ retailers and manufacturers, including Wayfair, Ashley Furniture, But and JJA Group, and it is backed by Partech and Y Combinator. Pricing. Credit-based. The Free plan gives 60 credits a month (about 20 images or 2 videos), no card required. Pro is $49/month for 500 credits; one image is 3 credits, one video 30, and unused credits roll over for a month on monthly plans. Some third-party roundups still show Presti's older furniture-era pricing in the hundreds of dollars; the figures here are from Presti's own site. Best for: brand, ecommerce and content teams producing image and video across many products and channels, where consistency and throughput matter more than one-off manual control. Where it falls short: the agent approach is more than a hobbyist editing one product a month needs; for a quick phone cutout, a lighter mobile tool is faster. Like any generative tool, complex or highly reflective products can need a second pass, and the API's finer implementation details are best confirmed with the team for a specific integration. Photoroom: the fast, mobile-first editor for sellers What it is. Photoroom is an AI product photography app built around speed and simplicity, on mobile and web. It started as a background remover and grew into a full commerce toolkit: AI backgrounds, Product Staging, Virtual Model, Ghost Mannequin, Flat Lay and AI Shadows, with category-tuned models. It also offers a separate REST API with Zapier and Make integrations, and reports more than 150 million downloads. Pricing. Among the cheapest serious options. Free includes watermarked, non-commercial exports. On standard monthly billing, Pro is $9.99/month (about $5.99 effective on annual billing) and includes up to 1,600 AI image generations plus a pool of AI credits; Max is $26.99/month (up to 5,000 generations) and adds the video generator; Ultra is $99/month (up to 15,000 generations) and unlocks 4K; a custom Enterprise plan sits above. On the lower tiers, 4K and adjustable AI shadows are gated, batch has per-session limits (50 on Pro, 250 on Max), and the API is billed separately per image. Prices shown on the US site in USD; the France site lists Pro at 9.99€. Best for: solo founders and small to mid Shopify or marketplace brands who want clean, marketplace-ready images from a phone. Where it falls short: AI lifestyle scenes can look artificial on complex or reflective products, and the $9.99 headline hides real costs once AI credits, batch caps and separate API billing stack up. Flair AI: a creative canvas for hands-on control What it is. Flair AI gives you a drag-and-drop scene canvas: arrange your product alongside props and 3D assets, then adjust lighting and camera angle before generating. It also covers AI fashion models and a human builder, virtual try-on, upscaling, variations, short AI product videos, bulk generation, reusable templates and real-time team collaboration, with an API on higher tiers. Pricing. Freemium, on monthly billing: Free ($0, 5 generated images), Pro ($10), Pro+ ($35, 80 generated images, adds a commercial license), Scale ($55, Tier 1 = 150 generated images, with API early access and higher tiers on a slider), and a custom Enterprise plan. The commercial license only starts at Pro+, and video generations are metered per tier (2 on Pro, 3 on Pro+, 5 on Scale). Best for: marketers, designers and agencies who want to art-direct a shot and produce ad creatives and social variations at pace. Where it falls short: product fidelity is a known weak point, with more risk of distortion on fine text or reflective surfaces, so test your hardest product first. Mokker AI: fast studio and white-background shots What it is. Mokker AI is a product-photo generator focused on one job done well: upload a single photo, and it removes the background and drops the product into a clean, category-aware studio or lifestyle scene, with realistic shadows, reflections and lighting. It ships 100+ templates, batch processing for whole catalogs, and high-resolution, print-ready output, and it slots into Amazon and Shopify listing workflows. Founded in 2019 (as Zerolens), Mokker is used by 350,000+ brands and was acquired by soona in 2024; it still runs standalone at mokker.ai . Pricing. A free plan gives 20 one-time photos with full studio and template access, no card. Starter is $13/month, Team is $29/user/month (500 photos, high-quality export, custom prompts), and Organization starts at about $83.25/user/month for 5+ seats with unlimited photos. Annual billing saves roughly 35%. Best for: sellers who need fast, reliable studio and white-background images at volume, especially for marketplace main images. Where it falls short: it is deliberately narrow. There is no on-model try-on and no video, and background variety is more limited than a drag-and-drop editor, so it works best as one tool in a stack rather than a complete solution. The API is in early access. Rewarx Studio: a full studio suite tuned by industry What it is. Rewarx Studio is a broad AI product photography suite that markets itself as fine-tuned for 20-plus industries (electronics, cosmetics, fashion, jewelry, home decor, beverages), with control over lighting, depth and material textures. Its modules span an AI Photography Studio, AI Model Studio (on-model with realistic shadows), AI Ghost Mannequin, AI Virtual Try-on, AI Mockup Generator, AI Group Shot Studio, background removal and an AI Product Page Builder that outputs a full listing asset set in one click. It targets 4K commercial assets and batch production for Amazon, Shopify, Etsy and eBay. Pricing. Credit-based, billed in euros, with a free trial. On monthly billing: Starter 9.90€ (100 credits), Growth 54.90€ (200 credits, bulk-optimized), Scale 129.90€ (500 credits, multi-SKU) and Agency 249.90€ (1,000 credits, API access, multi-user). The credit model is transparent: 1 credit is a standard 1K image, a 4K image is 3 credits, and a video is 20 credits, so a plan's real image capacity depends on the resolution and mix you choose. Best for: catalog teams that want one suite covering on-model, ghost mannequin, mockups and listing assets, with industry-specific tuning. Where it falls short: the lack of public pricing makes it hard to budget before a sales conversation because you need to create an account first, and a broad feature set means some modules are stronger than others, so test the specific module you need. Feature-by-feature comparison Legend: “ ✓” available on an official source, “ —” not offered or not a listed feature, Checked August 10, 2026. Feature Claid AI Presti Photoroom Flair AI Mokker AI Rewarx Background removal ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ AI backgrounds & scenes ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Lifestyle / staged scenes ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ On-model / AI fashion models ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ — ✓ Ghost mannequin — — ✓ — — ✓ Virtual try-on — — — ✓ — ✓ Product video ✓ ✓ Max+ tier ✓ — ✓ Upscaling / max resolution Up to 4K Up to 8K Up to 4K ✓ High-res Up to 4K Batch processing ✓ ✓ 50–250/session ✓ ✓ ✓ Brand kit / consistency ✓ ✓ ✓ Templates Templates Templates Team collaboration Limited ✓ Team Spaces ✓ real-time Seats (Team/Org) Multi-user (Agency) API access ✓ ✓ ✓ separate Higher tiers Early access only Agency plan Ecommerce publishing / import Via API Data import Shopify (Max+) — Listing workflow Page builder Platforms Web Web Mobile + Web Web Web Web Multi-model orchestration — ✓ — — — — Which tool by industry The right pick shifts with what you sell. Here is where each type of catalog tends to land, based on how each tool is built and positioned. Fashion and apparel: you need on-model or ghost-mannequin output. Claid AI, Flair AI and Rewarx all generate on-model shots; Photoroom and Rewarx handle ghost mannequin. [placeholder: an on-model example] Beauty and cosmetics: small, often reflective items where fidelity and clean studio backgrounds win. Mokker AI for fast white-background shots, Claid AI when label accuracy is critical. Home, decor and furniture: lifestyle context sells the product. Presti and Rewarx generate room-context scenes at scale; Flair AI when you want to art-direct the set. Food and beverage: appetizing lifestyle scenes and reflective surfaces. Mokker's category-aware scenes and Claid AI's fidelity both fit; test reflections carefully. High-volume marketplace catalogs: batch throughput and consistency dominate. Presti for image and video at scale, Claid AI for fidelity across many SKUs, Photoroom Ultra for high-volume mobile prep. Where AI still struggles AI product photography has closed most of the gap with a studio, but a few things still trip up every tool on this list, and they are worth knowing before you trust a generated hero image. Texture and draping. Changing how a fabric falls, folds or catches light convincingly still takes many iterations; generators drift on weave, sheen and drape. Exact dimensions with multiple products. When several items share one frame, keeping each one's real proportions and scale accurate is unreliable, so size relationships can quietly break. This matters commercially: Baymard found 42% of shoppers use a product's images to judge its size, so a scale error is a conversion risk, not just a cosmetic one. Precise positioning. Placing a product in an exact, repeatable position, for a template, a set or a brand layout, is hard to pin down; small shifts creep in between generations. These are industry-wide limits, not one tool's flaw. At Presti, they are exactly what our skills system is built to tame: reusable, brand-specific rules that constrain the output and, with a few iterations, bring texture, scale and positioning much closer to what a catalog actually needs. One more thing to plan for: transparency. Getty Images reports that nearly 90% of consumers want to know when an image was created with AI, so build disclosure into your marketplace and ad workflows rather than bolting it on later. How to choose List your jobs first. Cutouts only, or do you need lifestyle, on-model and video? The matrix tells you which tools qualify. Match to scale. A solo shop wants a cheap mobile editor (Photoroom, Mokker); a growing brand wants fidelity and consistency (Claid AI, Presti); an agency wants creative control (Flair AI); a broad catalog wants a full suite (Rewarx, Presti). Test your hardest product. Run a reflective, detailed or logo-heavy item through your shortlist before committing. Read the pricing page twice. Credits, batch caps, extra resolution and separately billed APIs are where the real cost hides. Pick one tool for your primary use case, prove it on your real catalog, and add a second only when volume justifies it. Subscribing to everything at once is the most common and most expensive mistake we see. Frequently asked questions What is the best AI product photography tool in 2026? There is no single best tool. Photoroom and Mokker AI lead on fast, cheap studio and cutout work, Claid AI leads on fidelity, Flair AI on creative control, Rewarx on breadth of studio modules, and Presti on producing image and video at scale. Match the tool to your volume, channels and the jobs you actually run. How much do AI product photography tools cost? Entry pricing in 2026 runs from free (usually watermarked or capped) to around $50/month for team plans, with some suites priced only on request. Photoroom starts at $9.99/month, Flair AI from about $10, Claid AI from about $15, Mokker AI at $13, Rewarx Studio from about ~$11 (9.90€) and Presti at $49/month for 500 credits with a free tier. Watch credits and separate API fees, since the headline price rarely reflects your true cost at volume. Can AI product photography replace a real photo shoot? For much routine catalog work, yes: clean packshots, lifestyle scenes and on-model shots are well within reach. Hero imagery for high-consideration products, where fine texture and materiality drive the purchase, can still benefit from a real shoot. Most teams blend the two, using AI for volume and photography for the flagship few. Are AI-generated product photos allowed on Amazon and other marketplaces? Generally yes, as long as the image accurately represents the actual product and follows each marketplace's rules, such as a pure white background and no watermarks on the main image. Lifestyle and secondary images face fewer restrictions. Check the current guidelines for each channel; Amazon's public guide to product photos is a good starting point. Which AI product photography tool is best for fashion and on-model shots? For on-model output, Claid AI, Flair AI, Rewarx Studio and Presti all generate garments on AI models, and Photoroom and Rewarx offer ghost-mannequin effects. Claid AI is the safer pick when preserving fabric detail and logos matters; Flair AI suits art-directed campaign shots. Always test with your actual garment, since fine prints and lettering are the hardest thing for AI to keep accurate. Which tool is best for a large catalog? For large catalogs, batch throughput, visual consistency and API access matter more than any single feature. Presti is built to produce image and video across many SKUs while staying consistent, Claid AI delivers fidelity at volume with an API, and Mokker AI re-backgrounds whole catalogs fast. Weigh batch caps and per-image economics, and run a representative slice before committing. Sources : each vendor's official pricing and product pages, read on August 10, 2026. Prices vary by region, promotion and app store and may change. Items marked [verify] were not confirmed on an official page and should be checked before publishing. This article reflects the Presti team's research and category experience and is not financial or legal advice.

title: Sunrun Prices $267 Million Securitization of Residential Solar and Storage Assets
summary: SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sunrun (Nasdaq: RUN), America’s largest provider of home battery storage, solar, and…...
body_text: Sunrun Prices $267 Million Securitization of Residential Solar and Storage Assets August 04, 2026 6:00 PM EDT Download as PDF SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sunrun (Nasdaq: RUN), America’s largest provider of home battery storage, solar, and home-to-grid power plants, today announced it has priced a securitization of leases and power purchase agreements. The securitization is Sunrun’s seventeenth securitization since 2015 and second issuance in 2026. “This $267 million public securitization involves refinancing a seasoned portfolio of residential solar assets. We appreciate our financial partners’ continued confidence in our high quality assets and servicing standards,” said Danny Abajian, Sunrun’s Chief Financial Officer. “This securitization was raised with Class A notes being priced at a 200 basis point credit spread, a 20 basis point improvement from the public Class A-1 Notes in Sunrun’s April 2026 securitization.” The securitization was structured with one class of A- rated notes (the “Class A Notes”) and one class of BB- rated notes (the “Class B Notes”). The Class B Notes were retained by Sunrun. The $267 million Class A Notes were marketed in a public asset backed securitization. The Class A Notes were priced with a coupon of 6.28%. The pricing of the Class A Notes reflects a spread of 200 basis points and a 6.33% yield. The initial balance of the Class A Notes represents a 74.2% advance rate on ADSAB (present value using a 7.5% discount rate). The Class A Notes have an expected weighted average life of 4.94 years, an Optional Redemption Date of July 30, 2035, and a final maturity date of January 30, 2054. The notes are backed by a diversified portfolio of 37,595 systems distributed across 42 utility service territories in 13 states. The weighted average customer FICO is 756. The transaction is expected to close by the end of August. BofA Securities was the sole structuring agent and served as joint bookrunner with Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, and RBC Capital Markets. KeyBanc Capital Markets and First Citizens Capital Securities served as co-managers for the securitization. This press release does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of such jurisdiction. About Sunrun Sunrun Inc. (Nasdaq: RUN) is America’s largest provider of home battery storage, solar, and home-to-grid power plants. As the pioneer of home energy systems offered through a no-upfront-cost subscription model, Sunrun empowers customers nationwide with greater energy control, security, and independence. Sunrun supports the grid by providing on-demand dispatchable power that helps prevent blackouts and lowers energy costs. Learn more at www.sunrun.com . title: Commerce now moves at the speed of culture. And anyone can move with it.
summary: Entrepreneurs turn culture's biggest moments into something you can hold. New data shows how fast they do it, and how it shapes the way we live and connect.
body_text: by Shopify Data Science Entrepreneurs turn culture's biggest moments into something you can hold. New data shows how fast they do it, and how it shapes the way we live and connect. The distance between a cultural moment and a business built on it used to be measured in weeks or months. Now it's hours. Sometimes even minutes. Starting a business and reaching that first sale has never been faster or more open to more people. It means a seller can respond to a cultural moment almost as it happens. And that becomes the enabling condition for everything else. In 2025, nearly 10% of new shops made their first sale within a single day of signing up, an increase of 43% in just three years. Half of all new sellers now reach their first sale within about three weeks. On May 8, 2025, white smoke rose over the Sistine Chapel and the world learned the name of the new pope. Within an hour, you could buy a T-shirt emblazoned with "da pope." One of the shops selling Pope Leo gear was Obvious Shirts , run by Joe Johnson, a Chicago entrepreneur who'd started years earlier making one-liner shirts for Cubs fans. He didn't have a manufacturing deal or a warehouse full of inventory waiting on a papal conclave. He had an idea, a storefront, and the instinct to move fast. For most of retail history, turning a moment into a product meant already having capital, inventory, manufacturing relationships, and shelf space. The moment would pass long before an ordinary person could act on it. Today, commerce can move at the speed of culture. Entrepreneurs are now the fastest translators between culture and the economy, taking the moments we witness and turning them into something we can hold. And you no longer have to already be in business to do it. When the time from idea to income narrows, high-agency people can act on an idea fast, whether they're starting something new or already running a shop. As those barriers keep falling, less and less stands between spotting a moment and selling into it. Moving at the speed of the moment A century ago, sociologist Émile Durkheim studied why people gather for rituals and named the energy that builds when a crowd experiences something together: collective effervescence . He noticed that the feeling needs somewhere to live once everyone goes home, so it attaches itself to an object, a totem, that lets people carry the belonging with them. A championship tee or a World Cup scarf is a totem in that sense. Commerce is how an experience gets a physical form. It takes a moment you'd otherwise just watch on a screen and makes it something you can touch, wear, and stand inside of. That's the difference between witnessing a moment and belonging to it. And why merch is so enduring. Sports are the purest test of speed, because there's a shared, public time stamp. Everyone knows the exact minute the final whistle, the buzzer-beater, or the trophy lift happened, so it’s easy to see how quickly commerce catches up. During the New York Knicks' 2026 playoff run, more than 3,000 shops listed orange-and-blue products, and the typical one made its first sale within three days. Then there's the World Cup, which wrapped in July and created breakout moments faster than anyone could plan for. When an underdog became the tournament's improbable hero, people around the world reached for a way to celebrate him. Sellers kept pace, half of them making a first sale within three days, this time for fans spread across continents. And then a certain soccer player wandered into Wild Bill's Western Store , a family-run shop in downtown Dallas, and walked out with a taxidermied raccoon clutching a whiskey bottle. The image went viral, and since that June visit Wild Bill's online sales rose 10x compared to a month earlier. The owners switched on global shipping for the first time. When a trend becomes a category The same low barriers that let someone catch a one-week wave also build lasting categories. Take matcha. It didn't explode overnight. It was a wellness habit, then an aesthetic, then a genuine staple. A wave of independent brands launched or expanded alongside it, from Morning Made in Australia to Matcha Mystic in the Netherlands. When the craze peaked in 2025, nearly 1,500 new shops launched to meet it. The easy assumption is that they would disappear when the hype cooled. Instead the majority of them (70%) are still active today, with most reaching their first sale within about two weeks of listing a product. What started as a trend is becoming a category, with sales continuing to climb quarter over quarter. As protein changed from a bodybuilder's obsession to a number that all shoppers scan for on the back of a package, entrepreneurs met the moment. Over the past year, protein coffee sales climbed 507% and prepared protein foods 194%, while traditional protein shakes fell 40%. Sellers moved in to meet this shift in demand, with 76% more shops selling protein coffee and 37% more selling prepared protein foods year over year, each with its own idea of what a protein product can be, from ramen to cereal. Both of these were dismissed as passing trends until, at some point no one can quite name, they became the default. The barriers are collapsing The time it takes to reach that first sale keeps shrinking, and that helps entrepreneurs whether they're building for a moment or building for a decade. The sooner someone makes a sale, the sooner they know the idea works. Now the distance between what culture wants and what an entrepreneur can deliver has disappeared. Share this story: Twitter Facebook Email Read more The preparedness paradox: Wait for “ready,” and it might never come The data says founders would do it again. Even in this economy. Entrepreneurship has no zip code

title: Credicorp enhances and modernizes IT infrastructure with Kyndryl
summary: The collaboration strengthens operational resilience and agility through a scalable, cloud‑ready technology model powered by Kyndryl Bridge and AI
body_text: LIMA, Peru, August 18, 2026 — Kyndryl (NYSE: KD), a leading provider of mission‑critical enterprise technology services, and Credicorp , the leading financial services holding company in Peru, with operations in Chile, Colombia, Bolivia, and Panama, today announced a new collaboration to modernize the group’s technology environment with cloud and AI and standardize management across Credicorp’s companies. By incorporating AI-enabled operations, this project will help anticipate incidents, optimize performance and support continuous improvement across all group companies, strengthening resilience as well as the availability and continuity of the digital services they provide to their customers. Large financial services groups face increasing pressure to operate resilient and scalable technology environments while managing legacy complexity and costs. To address these challenges, Credicorp worked with Kyndryl to co-create and implement a corporate technology management model that reduces fragmentation across operating companies, strengthens connectivity and enables better use of shared data and insights across the group. The new model is designed to support long-term modernization and cloud migration under the direction of Kyndryl Consult . “As a diversified financial group, we needed a technology model that could scale across our companies while maintaining operational stability,” said André Rezende, Credicorp Corporate CTO. “Working with Kyndryl will allow us to move toward a unified approach to technology management, improving efficiency, reducing complexity and strengthening our ability to respond to changing business demands.” “Modernization initiatives in complex, regulated environments require a careful balance between transformation and operational continuity,” said Rodolfo Armellini, Managing Director, Kyndryl Latin America Southwest. “Our work with Credicorp shows how a collaborative and scalable operating model — supported by AI‑driven operations — can reduce complexity, improve efficiency and establish a strong foundation for cloud adoption, while maintaining operational stability.” As part of the initiative, Kyndryl will leverage Kyndryl Bridge , its AI‑powered, open‑integration digital platform, to help Credicorp integrate, observe and orchestrate its technology environment. The corporate model aligns Credicorp’s strategic leadership with execution across its companies, supported by dedicated technical teams. By standardizing processes, increasing automation and consolidating service management under a single operating framework, Credicorp is addressing growth-related challenges such as managing diverse technology environments, while accelerating time to market for new capabilities and better preparing the group for future cloud migrations. The collaboration builds on Kyndryl’s experience supporting large enterprises with complex technology environments and reflects a shared focus on long-term resilience, efficiency and continuous modernization — helping Credicorp strengthen the technology backbone that supports secure, reliable and scalable services for its customers. About Credicorp Credicorp (NYSE: BAP) is the leading financial services holding company in Peru with presence in Chile, Colombia, Bolivia, and Panama and United States. Credicorp has a diversified business portfolio organized into four lines of business (“LoBs”): Universal Banking, through BCP and Banco de Crédito de Bolivia; Microfinance, through Mibanco in Peru and Colombia; Insurance & Pension Funds, through Grupo Pacifico and Prima AFP; and Investment Management & Advisory, through Credicorp Capital, Wealth Management at BCP and ASB Bank Corp. Additionally, it complements its operations through Krealo, its Corporate Venture Capital arm. For more information, visit www.grupocredicorp.com . About Kyndryl Kyndryl (NYSE: KD) is a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services, offering advisory, implementation and managed service capabilities to thousands of customers in more than 60 countries. As the world’s largest IT infrastructure services provider, the company designs, builds, manages and modernizes the complex information systems that the world depends on every day. For more information, visit www.kyndryl.com . Kyndryl press contact press@kyndryl.com

title: Why orchestration matters in modern customer communications
summary: Learn why orchestration matters in modern customer communications and how it helps connect workflows, channels, compliance, and delivery.
body_text: More channels and tools do not automatically create better customer communication. Without coordination, these channels and tools create more systems to manage, more manual work, and more opportunities for messages to become delayed, inconsistent, or disconnected from the customer’s situation. That disconnect often becomes more visible after acquisition. According to IDC , organizations invest heavily in winning customers, but the systems and processes that support them afterward frequently operate in silos, creating friction across customer touchpoints . Communication orchestration brings those moving parts together. It coordinates data, content, workflows, business rules, and channels so organizations can work more efficiently, respond faster, and deliver communications that support both business priorities and the customer journey. What is orchestration? Communication orchestration is the process of coordinating the end-to-end lifecycle of customer communications . Instead of managing documents, emails, SMS messages, and print communications through separate systems, orchestration brings these processes together into a unified workflow. A typical communication workflow may include: Collecting customer and business data Generating personalized documents or messages Applying business rules and compliance requirements Selecting the appropriate delivery channel Monitoring delivery status and outcomes By connecting these steps, organizations can create more streamlined and reliable communication processes. Why traditional communication processes fall short Many organizations have built their communication systems over time, often adding new tools as business needs evolve. While these systems may work independently, they frequently create challenges when used together. Common issues include: Limited visibility into communication workflows Manual processes that increase the risk of errors Inconsistent messaging across channels Delays caused by disconnected systems Difficulty demonstrating compliance during audits These challenges become even more significant as communication volumes grow, and customers expect faster, more personalized interactions. The benefits of automating communication orchestration Automating communication orchestration helps organizations reduce repetitive tasks while improving consistency. Instead of manually managing each stage of the communication process, predefined workflows can automatically route data, generate documents, and trigger delivery based on business rules. Automated orchestration can help organizations: Reduce manual processing time Improve communication consistency Minimize human error Accelerate response times Scale communication operations as demand grows This allows employees to spend less time managing routine tasks and more time focusing on customer needs. Why visibility is essential Creating communications is only part of the process. Organizations also need visibility into how those communications are performing. Visibility extends beyond delivery metrics. Organizations need to understand behavioral signals, service interactions, and engagement patterns across the customer journey to determine the next best action and identify issues before customers disengage. Operational dashboards and monitoring tools provide valuable insights, including: Communication volumes Processing times Delivery success rates Workflow bottlenecks Resource utilization Access to real-time information enables teams to identify issues early, improve operational efficiency, and make informed decisions based on data rather than assumptions. Ensuring reliable delivery Even well-designed communications provide little value if they never reach the intended recipient. Modern communication strategies often use multiple delivery channels—including email, SMS, mobile notifications, print, and customer portals—to maximize reach. Some organizations also implement fallback strategies that automatically switch to an alternative channel if the primary delivery method fails. This multi-channel approach helps ensure important messages reach customers while improving the overall customer experience. Supporting compliance and transparency Many regulated industries, including insurance, financial services, and governments, must meet strict regulatory requirements for customer communications. Governance becomes even more important as more organizations introduce AI into communication workflows . Effective AI-powered orchestration depends on trusted data, approved content, customer context, and clear operating rules. Without those foundations, organizations risk inconsistent messaging, compliance failures, and poor customer experiences. A well-orchestrated communication process can help organizations: Maintain consistent messaging Track communication history Document approval processes Monitor delivery status Create audit trails for regulatory reporting These capabilities make it easier to demonstrate compliance while reducing operational risk. Turn communications into connected experiences Communication orchestration provides a structured approach to coordinating these interactions, helping businesses improve efficiency, maintain consistency, and deliver a better customer experience. Rather than viewing communication as a series of disconnected tasks, organizations can think of it as a connected journey —one that begins with accurate data, follows a well-defined workflow, and ends with the right message reaching the right customer at the right time. summary: The new enterprise offering combines CLEAR+, CLEAR Concierge, TSA PreCheck® enrollment, and the CLEAR mobile app into a seamless corporate…...
body_text: The new enterprise offering combines CLEAR+, CLEAR Concierge, TSA PreCheck® enrollment, and the CLEAR mobile app into a seamless corporate travel program designed to set a new standard for business travel. NEW YORK , Aug. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CLEAR (NYSE: YOU), the secure identity company, announced the launch of CLEAR Corporate Memberships, an industry-first enterprise offering that gives companies a seamless way to support business travelers through the entire day of travel. Making its formal debut at the Global Business Travel Association (GBTA) Convention 2026 in Chicago, CLEAR Corporate Memberships brings together CLEAR+, CLEAR Concierge, TSA PreCheck® enrollment, and the CLEAR app into a single corporate program designed to help business travelers move with greater speed, certainty, and predictability from home to gate. Business travel is increasingly unpredictable and volatile. According to industry research , nearly nine in ten business travelers experienced travel disruptions in 2025, and U.S. companies spend an estimated $17 billion annually managing the impact of delays and cancellations. Travel day uncertainty leads to lost productivity, increased stress for travelers and travel managers, and negative impacts to employee engagement and retention. While organizations carefully plan and invest heavily in managing travel, the day-of-travel experience remains largely overlooked. CLEAR Corporate Memberships is designed to help business travelers gain greater transparency, control and efficiency to the travel experience. The result is companies achieving improved productivity, increased engagement and lower travel costs. "Business travelers deserve every opportunity to make their trips more predictable and efficient," said Michael Barkin, President of CLEAR. "Companies invest significant resources getting employees where they need to be, yet the day of travel remains uncertain, leading to stress and underutilized time. CLEAR Corporate Memberships deliver the tools that business travelers need to deliver the best results for their organizations with the least friction in their travel. With CLEAR, the new standard of travel is seamless." CLEAR Corporate Memberships include: A seamless home-to-gate experience with a CLEAR+ membership, including access to CLEAR's airport eGates: Every enrolled employee gets a full CLEAR+ membership, using biometric identity verification and eGate technology to move through security in seconds. The CLEAR app: Real-time security wait times, airport traffic patterns, and gate distances, so employees can plan their travel day before they leave home, the office, or a meeting. CLEAR Concierge: A dedicated CLEAR Ambassador can be booked to meet travelers, handle bags, and escort them through security all the way to the gate — the fastest way through the airport, with none of the stress. TSA PreCheck® enrollment, with in-person support: On-site enrollment events and travel fairs for both CLEAR and TSA PreCheck®, so employees can enroll without leaving the workplace. Seamless personal travel: With CLEAR membership, employees can use the same eGates, app, and Concierge access on their own trips, supporting employee satisfaction and retention. CLEAR Corporate Memberships brings the company's trusted travel offerings into a single enterprise program, helping companies support employees across the full day of travel with predictability, ease, and speed. For more information about CLEAR Corporate Memberships, visit CLEAR Corporate Travel . About CLEAR The mission of CLEAR, the secure identity company, is to strengthen security and create frictionless experiences. With over 43 million Members and a growing network of partners across the world, CLEAR's secure identity platform is transforming the way people live, work, and travel. Whether you are traveling, at the stadium, or on your phone, CLEAR connects you to the things that make you, you—making everyday experiences easier, more secure, and friction-free. CLEAR is committed to privacy done right. Members are always in control of their own information, and we do not sell biometric or sensitive personal data. For more information, visit clearme.com. title: Upstart Publishes July 2026 Originations and Latest UMI
summary: BURLINGAME, Calif. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 3, 2026-- Upstart Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: UPST), the leading artificial intelligence (AI) lending marketplace, today published its monthly origination volume for July 2026 and its latest Upstart Macro Index (UMI) reading.
body_text: Upstart Publishes July 2026 Originations and Latest UMI August 3, 2026 PDF Version BURLINGAME, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 3, 2026-- Upstart Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: UPST), the leading artificial intelligence (AI) lending marketplace, today published its monthly origination volume for July 2026 and its latest Upstart Macro Index (UMI) reading. For historical data and more information, see upstart.com/volume and upstart.com/umi . Monthly Origination Volume Period Originations Origination days Originations, Dollars per day July 2026 $1,397.4M 27.4 $51.0M August 3, 2026 UMI The current UMI is 1.50, up slightly from the July 8, 2026 reading of 1.49, and is the highest level since January 2026. For reference, a UMI of 1.50 is approximately 50% above what Upstart would expect in a normal economy (a UMI of 1.0), up from about 49% above normal in the prior reading. UMI has remained above 1.0 since early 2022, reflecting a sustained period of elevated default risk relative to Upstart's long-run baseline, but remains below the series' peak of 1.68, reached in 2024. About Upstart Origination Volume “Originations” refers to Transaction Volume, Dollars, one of the key operating metrics Upstart reports in its quarterly and annual filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”). Transaction Volume, Dollars is defined as the total principal amount of loan originations (or committed amounts for HELOCs and draws for Cash Line) facilitated through Upstart’s marketplace during the periods presented. “Origination days” represent the effective number of funding days in a month, based on a 24-hour funding window starting and ending at approximately 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Each business day counts as 1.0 day in Upstart’s calculation. Weekend days and bank holidays are weighted at 0.55 days to reflect lower application activity and are rolled forward to the next business day, when those loans are typically funded. If month-end falls on a weekend or bank holiday, originations from that period are attributed to the following month. “Originations, Dollars per day” is calculated as total “Originations” divided by the number of “Origination days” in the applicable period. See upstart.com/volume for more information. About UMI The Upstart Macro Index (UMI) estimates the impact of the macroeconomy on credit losses for Upstart-powered loans. The UMI is a simplified representation, using Upstart's personal loan data, of the full suite of models and techniques Upstart has developed for assessing macroeconomic risk in lending. These may be used to different extents in the underwriting of each loan product, with personal loans generally using them most fully. Upstart regularly recalibrates its underwriting model based on its latest read of macroeconomic conditions, and the published UMI is a close proxy for that read. Each new UMI reading is meant to give investors and capital partners a view into two things: (1) the macroeconomic risk assumptions currently factored into the pricing and approval of new loans, and (2) a directional sense of how Upstart's existing loans are performing — which depends largely on the actual risk level assumed when those loans were originally underwritten. See upstart.com/umi for more information. About Upstart Upstart (NASDAQ: UPST) is the leading AI lending marketplace, connecting millions of consumers to more than 100 banks and credit unions that leverage Upstart’s AI models and cloud applications to deliver superior credit products. With Upstart AI, lenders can approve more borrowers at lower rates while delivering the exceptional digital-first experience customers demand. More than 90% of loans are fully automated, with no human intervention by Upstart. Founded in 2012, Upstart’s platform includes personal loans, automotive loans, home equity lines of credit, and Upstart’s new Cash Line product, a revolving line of credit. Upstart is based in Burlingame, California. Legal Disclaimer The Originations and Originations, Dollars per day data (“Originations Data”) provided in this press release are unaudited, preliminary, and subject to completion of our financial closing procedures in connection with our quarterly financial results as reported in our filings with the SEC, which are also available on our Investor Relations website. While Originations Data have historically been the largest predictor of our total revenue, this historical correlation is not a guaranteed indicator for future final results. The Originations Data are presented without commentary and should be read together with our quarterly and annual financial results and our filings with the SEC. Past UMI performance can provide no assurance and is not indicative of future UMI results. UMI is based on historical data and Upstart’s analysis of the losses within Upstart-powered loan portfolios and is specific to Upstart’s borrower base. UMI is not intended to measure the macroeconomic risks in terms of losses of loan portfolios or asset classes that are not Upstart-powered loans, including loans held by other segments of the U.S. population. It is not designed to measure the current state of the overall economy or to measure or predict future macroeconomic conditions, trends or risks. While UMI may provide a directional sense of how Upstart's existing loans are performing, it is also not designed to measure or predict the future performance of Upstart-powered loans or of Upstart’s other products, overall financial results of operations or stock price. We expect that our research and development efforts to improve UMI could result in changes or revisions to current or past UMI values or to our UMI methodology in the future. All forward-looking statements or information in this press release are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from those that Upstart expected. Any forward-looking statements or information are only as of the date hereof. Upstart undertakes no obligation to update or revise any forward-looking statements as a result of new information, future events or otherwise. More information about these risks and uncertainties is provided in Upstart’s public filings with the SEC, copies of which may be obtained by visiting Upstart’s investor relations website at ir.upstart.com or the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov . title: Redwire Successfully Completes Critical Design Review for ELSA Solar Arrays for National Security Program with Moog
summary: Redwire announced that is has successfully completed critical design review (CDR) for ELSA solar arrays for an undisclosed national security program in Low Earth Orbit, through a contract with Moog…
body_text: Redwire announced that is has successfully completed critical design review (CDR) for ELSA solar arrays for an undisclosed national security program in Low Earth Orbit, through a contract with Moog Inc. This milestone paves the way for manufacturing and integration with Moog Inc.’s METEOR satellite bus. Through a contract with Moog announced in March 2026, Redwire is responsible for the system design, manufacturing, testing, and flight hardware delivery of the ELSA solar array wings. ELSA has also been baselined by Moog as a standard component of their METEOR ESPA-Grande satellite bus. The bus is all-orbit capable and supports a wide variety of missions and flight profiles, including pathfinder constellation missions and other disaggregated architectures. The CDR confirmed that ELSA’s design has undergone a rigorous and detailed assessment and is in full compliance with customer requirements for the program. ELSA is designed for customers who need to minimize solar array stowed volume and mass, while remaining competitive with conventional solar array performance and pricing. The solution provides 50% more power by volume than traditional solar arrays. Engineered for volume production, ELSA offers a step function improvement in modular, scalable design and rapid turnaround to drive down cost and improve delivery times. Redwire is a market leader in space power solutions, with a proven track record of innovation and on-orbit success. Redwire-built solar arrays have a 100% on-orbit success rate on flagship space missions including the International Space Station and NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test mission. Read more about the ELSA arrays for Moog here: Redwire Awarded Contract to Deliver ELSA High-Performance, Low-Mass Solar Arrays to Moog Inc. for National Security Program | Redwire

title: Adagio Medical Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
summary: LAGUNA HILLS, Calif. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 11, 2026-- Adagio Medical Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: ADGM) (“Adagio” or “the Company”), a leading innovator in catheter ablation technologies for the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias, today announced financial results for the second quarter ended June 30,
body_text: Adagio Medical Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results August 11, 2026 PDF Version LAGUNA HILLS, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 11, 2026-- Adagio Medical Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: ADGM) (“Adagio” or “the Company”), a leading innovator in catheter ablation technologies for the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias, today announced financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Recent Business Highlights: Announced the successful treatment at the Hospital of University of Pennsylvania of the first patient with the Company’s next-generation vCLAS™ Ultra Ultra-Low temperature ablation catheter (“ULTA”), which is designed to be faster and more maneuverable than the first generation vCLAS™ Ventricular Ablation System catheter, under Expanded Access authorization from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) Announced pivotal results from the 209-patient FULCRUM-VT trial, which were presented in a late-breaking session at Heart Rhythm Society 2026, demonstrating a promising safety profile with only 2.4% protocol-defined Major Adverse Events and six-month results of 84% freedom from implantable cardioverter defibrillator (“ICD”) shock and a 78% discontinuation or reduced dose of antiarrhythmic drugs, as well as equivalent results across both ischemic and non-ischemic cardiomyopathy patients with the Company's proprietary ULTA technology Submitted Premarket Approval (“PMA”) application, supported by the FULCRUM-VT pivotal IDE trial, to the FDA for the vCLAS Ventricular Ablation System for the treatment of drug-refractory, recurrent, sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia (“VT”) in patients with ischemic or non-ischemic structural heart disease “This quarter marked an inflection point for Adagio as our team continues to execute and deliver on our critical milestones. The enthusiastic physician reception of our FULCRUM-VT late-breaking data at HRS reinforced what we have long believed about the potential for this technology, and the successful treatment of the first patient with vCLAS Ultra — a particularly complex case — was a powerful proof point for our next-generation system,” said Todd Usen, Chief Executive Officer of Adagio Medical. “We believe our progress — combined with the breadth of our clinical evidence for both ischemic and non-ischemic patients — positions our fully-endocardial ULTA platform as a uniquely differentiated solution capable of treating the entire spectrum of cases in an addressable market that has long needed a purpose-built solution. We remain focused on executing against the milestones ahead as we work to bring our proprietary technology to the many patients who suffer from VT.” Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Cost of revenue was nil for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $0.3 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to the pause in commercial activity in Europe. Depreciation expense related to consoles loaned to customers is generally classified within cost of revenue; however, because the Company did not generate revenue during the three months ended June 30, 2026, such depreciation expense is reflected within research and development expenses for the period. Research and development expenses were $2.5 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $2.0 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to higher product development costs, including consulting and prototyping expenses, and higher operational costs, including the aforementioned depreciation expense, partially offset by lower clinical trial expenses. Selling, general and administrative expenses were $2.5 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $2.4 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to higher stock-based compensation expenses, partially offset by lower professional services expenses. Net loss for the three months ended June 30, 2026, was $6.7 million, or $(0.30) per share (Basic), compared to a net loss of $3.9 million, or $(0.26) per share (Basic), for the three months ended June 30, 2025. Weighted average shares of common stock outstanding, basic and diluted, were 22,210,459 as of June 30, 2026. The Company's fully diluted share count includes all outstanding warrants; however, for purposes of calculating net loss per share, warrants and certain other potentially dilutive securities are excluded as their inclusion would be anti-dilutive. Cash and cash equivalents were $7.7 million as of June 30, 2026. About Adagio Medical Holdings, Inc. Adagio is a medical device company focused on developing and commercializing products for the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias utilizing its novel, proprietary, catheter-based Ultra-Low temperature ablation (“ULTA,” formerly known as ULTC) technology. ULTA is designed to create large footprint, titratable lesions extending through the depth of both diseased and healthy cardiac tissue, all through an endocardial approach. The Company is currently focused on the treatment of ventricular arrhythmias with its purpose-built vCLAS Ventricular Ablation System, which is CE Marked, and in May 2026 the Company submitted the results of the FULCRUM-VT pivotal study to support its PMA application to the FDA for the vCLAS Ventricular Ablation System. The Company is also developing a next-generation vCLAS Ultra catheter, designed to support faster ablation procedures with a smaller and more flexible form factor than its predecessor vCLAS device. About FULCRUM VT FULCRUM-VT (Feasibility of Ultra-Low Temperature Cryoablation in Recurring Monomorphic Ventricular Tachycardia) is a prospective, multi-center, open-label, single-arm trial, which has fully enrolled 209 patients with structural heart disease of both ischemic and non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, indicated for catheter ablation of drug refractory VT in accordance with current treatment guidelines. FULCRUM-VT 6-month primary chronic effectiveness was defined as freedom from sustained monomorphic VT lasting longer than 30 seconds or VT requiring appropriate ICD device therapy, in the absence of new or increase in antiarrhythmic drug therapy beyond previously failed dose. The FDA has granted Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) approval to expand the Company’s FULCRUM-VT trial to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Company’s next-generation vCLAS Ultra catheter for the treatment of Sustained Monomorphic Ventricular Tachycardia (SMVT). Adagio’s vCLAS™ Ventricular Ablation System is commercially available for the treatment of monomorphic VT in Europe and select other geographies but is limited to investigational use in the United States. Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Words such as “anticipates,” “believes,” “expects,” “intends,” “projects,” “plans,” and “future” or similar expressions are intended to identify forward-looking statements. Forward-looking statements include statements concerning: Adagio’s strategy, future operations, future financial position, and projected expenses; the expected timing and results of Adagio's clinical trials, including the reproducibility of the favorable results initially seen in Adagio’s FULCRUM-VT pivotal data and the evaluation of the vCLAS Ultra catheter under the expanded IDE approval; the potential for ULTA technology to address unmet needs in the treatment of VT, including across both ischemic and non-ischemic cardiomyopathy substrates; and the potential for FDA approval of Adagio’s product candidates, including the PMA application for the vCLAS Ventricular Ablation System. title: Building Alai's growth from scratch: 88,000 signups as the first marketing hire
summary: Design and refine beautiful presentations instantly using Alai's AI presentation maker. Start free and turn your ideas into professional decks in seconds.
body_text: I joined Alai as the marketing lead back in November (2025). Eight months in, here’s a quick guide on the channels that helped me move the needle, the growth I saw and the strategy I used. We measured success via the following three metrics: Traffic. Getting the right people to the site without paying for every click. Signups. Getting that traffic to actually try the product. Signup-to-paid conversion. Getting those people to pay. I worked on three channels: Reddit, SEO, and branding (socials, product newsletters, Product Hunt launch). Our primary focus was to build strong organic levers of engagement through content. The growth, at a glance Metric I owned Start Finish Growth Monthly signups 4,062 (Nov) 21,680 over 5x Organic traffic / mo around 700 (Jan) 27,800 roughly 40x Measured search clicks / mo 7,020 (Jan) 21,200 roughly 3x Signup to paid conversion* around 1% (Nov) Between 2 to 2.5% roughly 2x *Conversion is worked out from the signup and paid ratios. Paid users grew too, close to 12x from November to the April peak. Paying customers came from Reddit and Google Search. Quality improved as volume grew. Pillar 1: Reddit Goal While exploring tools, most people usually search for some version of "what's the best app for X" or "has anyone actually used Y." A lot of that asking happens on Reddit, right at the moment someone is about to decide. The purpose was to show up for all the queries that mattered to us, in front of the people who were one good answer away from signing up. There's a second payoff too. LLMs lean heavily on Reddit, so the threads we engaged in reached two audiences at once: the people reading them, and LLMs that include Reddit citations. Strategy / What was done A few systems made this work: Finding the right threads before they went cold - We set up an automation that scanned Reddit for threads mentioning keywords related to what we do, and dropped the relevant ones into a Slack channel every morning, so we could engage while they were still active. I kept a running list of the subreddits that drove the most engagement for us, and rotated posts across them so we weren't leaning on the same community every time. The posting itself ran across three personas, each with its own voice: Founder: posting from the building-it side, as the person actually making the product. Brand: the official Alai account, holding the company line. Marketing: talking shop with other marketers, peer to peer. The accounts were also at different stages of maturity, so the established ones took the higher-stakes threads while newer ones spent time warming up and building a real posting history first. Across all three, the rule held: be useful before anything else. Every post had to teach or inform on its own merits, and Alai came up only when it genuinely answered the question, shown as one of several options someone might pick. The posts spanned formats and funnel stages: How-to guides and automation walkthroughs: top of funnel, pulling people in with something worth learning. Comparisons: for people weighing one tool against another. Listicles: for people close to choosing and scanning their options. To make all of this repeatable, I built a Claude skill with its own readme that drafts a post for each persona automatically, in the right voice. It turned a slow manual write into something I could spin up quickly and keep consistent across every account. Results By April, Reddit was sending around 5.3K unique visitors to the site a month, and one post pulled 460k views on its own. Those visitors became signups: Reddit-sourced signups went from under 100 a month in November to around 4,100 in April, our second-largest source by self-reported attribution, behind only Google Search. The bigger result was paying customers. Reddit became our single biggest source of them, ahead of search. So Reddit sat second for signups and first for paying customers, which means it converted better than any other channel. Pillar 2: SEO This is the channel with the clearest before-and-after, so it's worth walking through properly. Goal When I joined in November, under 1% of our search clicks came from non-branded queries. In plain terms, almost everyone who found us on Google had already typed our name. Anyone out there searching "best ai presentation maker" with no idea Alai existed simply wasn't running into us. So search was barely pulling its weight. It mostly worked as a login shortcut for people who already knew us. From January, the goal was to change that: make search a way for total strangers to discover Alai, across the whole funnel, and get Alai showing up inside AI answers while we were at it. Strategy / What was done Starting with the content closest to a signup. Signups were the primary goal, so I started at the middle and bottom of the funnel, where the search intent is closest to a decision. The first wave was: "Best [X]" listicles ranking the top tools in a category, which is exactly what people search right before they pick one. Detailed reviews and alternatives pages for the biggest tools in the space, to catch people already looking at a competitor: Gamma alternatives, Kimi alternatives, and so on. Trending topics as they broke, like creating and editing slides from NotebookLM, where a sudden spike in searches had almost no good content answering it yet. Top-of-funnel how-tos and utility tool pages (link-to-PPT, PDF-to-PPT, a deck prettifier) came in on top of that foundation once the commercial pages were ranking. Building authority with backlinks. None of my content would rank without domain authority, and authority comes mostly from backlinks. The usual routes are expensive agencies or pricey tools. I built my own lightweight system instead, and it ran on about $20: Agent 1 scrapes relevant blogs for my target keywords automatically. Agent 2 reads each blog and writes a personalized opening line for the outreach email. Everything flows into a Google Sheet with the email copy, follow-up sequences, and recipient info. An Apps Script sends the approved emails, tracks replies, and handles the follow-ups on its own. That system took our Domain Rating from 21 to 36 and our backlinks from 132 to 396. I wrote the whole thing up in a LinkedIn post , which then became its own backlink engine: people who read it reached out wanting to use it, and those were exactly the people actively participating in exchanges. Turning the first three months into a machine. By month three I had enough working patterns to systematize the whole content process into a chain of claude skills, each one handing off to the next: Keyword research: takes a topic and uses the Ahrefs MCP to run detailed keyword research, then passes it down the line. Brief generator: turns that into a full brief with outline, depth, keyword volumes, LLM snippet strategy, headline structure, and the backlink and interlink plan. SEO writer: a different writer for each content type, each trained on our existing blogs for tone and on our product files for accuracy. Humanisation pass: checks the draft for over-exaggeration and anything that reads as AI before it ships. Medium repurpose: spins each finished blog into a Medium version to widen reach. What used to take days of manual work became a pipeline I could run end to end. While these skills were my go-to for a strong first draft, I did always make it a point to do a heavy revision on all articles and each review was based on actual testing. Results The clearest way to see what changed is to watch how the branded and non-branded split moved. Search demand we captured Nov 2025 Jan 2026 Apr 2026 Share of clicks from non-branded queries under 1% 14% 41% Share of impressions from non-branded queries 5% 69% 92% Read it left to right. In November, search only worked if you knew the name. By January, with the first content live, we were already appearing for the big commercial searches even though we weren't winning many clicks yet, which is what 69% of impressions at 14% of clicks tells you. By April, 41% of our search clicks came from people who had never heard of Alai before they searched. One page did more of this than anything else. The "best AI presentation makers" listicle went from 115 clicks in January to 9,496 in April, and it now pulls close to 891,000 impressions a month. It's the biggest organic asset we have, and it ranks for the exact thing people search right before they choose a tool. The size of that move is easier to feel with the before-and-after. The term "ai presentation maker" sat at position 90 in November and 30 in January. By April the "best" versions of those terms were in the top 3. Cracking the top 3 for "best ai presentation maker," "best presentation maker ai," and "best ai for presentations," and landing right at the edge of it for "best ai ppt maker," were the biggest wins of the whole channel. Those are the searches a buyer makes right before they pick. When combined with our other blogs, the top-line numbers caught up. Measured search traffic, January to now: Metric Jan 2026 May 2026 Change Total clicks 7.02K 21.2K +14.2K (roughly 3x) Total impressions 458K 2.17M +1.71M (roughly 4.7x) Average position 9.7 7.1 improved by 2.6 Average CTR 1.5% 1.0% down 0.5pp The CTR dip is easy to misread. Impressions grew much faster than clicks because the top-of-funnel guides started ranking for a huge spread of new, browsy queries. More people seeing us, a smaller share clicking any single term, and a lot more clicks in total. The rankings and traffic that authority unlocked, from Ahrefs: Metric Jan 2026 Now Change Organic keywords 86 318 +232 Top-3 rankings 3 81 +78 Organic traffic / mo around 700 27.8K +27.1K Traffic value / mo around $200 $2.8K +$2.6K And the AI bet, starting from almost nothing: AI surface Before Now Google AI Mode 0 212 Google AI Overviews 0 180 Grok 0 755 Gemini 0 132 Perplexity 0 40 ChatGPT citations 9 15 The authority from the backlink work is what let the listicles climb from 3 top-3 rankings to 81. All of this lands where it counts, in signups. By April, Google Search was our single biggest source of signups, at roughly 6,800 a month, up from 1176 in Jan when we just started out on SEO. The AI-visibility work showed up in the same place: signups crediting AI chatbots climbed from around 40 to nearly 1,700. (Both come from the self-reported "how did you hear about us" field.) Pillar 3: Social and branding (socials and newsletter) Goal Of the three pillars, this was the one I kept lightest on purpose. Reddit and SEO were where the growth came from, so that's where most of my time went. The job here was narrower: keep a basic, consistent brand presence across the channels that mattered, and communicate well with the customers we already had. Same voice and look wherever someone ran into Alai, and a newsletter that kept existing users in the loop. Strategy / What was done The work split into three pieces. Product newsletter. We had a user base of over 100,000 people, and the newsletter kept them warm. On a bi-weekly to weekly cadence, each issue walked through new launches, how to actually use them, and ways to get more out of the product. The job was retention: bringing people who had already signed up back into the habit of using Alai. Socials. Every launch and update went out across our brand pages and our personal LinkedIn accounts, in one consistent voice. The clearest example is the most recent one. When we opened public access to Alai’s Modern Slides, I made the launch video using Claude Code, and every design in the campaign was made with Alai or Claude itself. You can see the launch post here . Product Hunt launch. My first ever Product Hunt launch! We finished the day in 4th place, with 314 upvotes and 58 comments. My biggest takeaway - spend a month engaging on other launches and PH in general and ask team members to do so as well! Results Two numbers track the branding side from November to April. Brand searches climbed as the name got known. People specifically Googling Alai went from around 2,100 branded clicks a month in November to over 10,500 by April, with the number of brand searches itself roughly doubling on top of that. More people knew the name well enough to type it. That recognition fed signups. Across LinkedIn, Instagram, and Twitter/X, social-driven signups went from around 550 a month in November to about 3,900 by April. The traffic mix backs it up. By April, "Direct / None" was the second-largest source of visitors behind Google, ahead of every referral. That's people typing us in or coming back with no tracked link. Wrapping Up: A few moments I’m proud of Taking the end of the blog to boast a little: 88,238 signups from November to June, off the back of three channels built from nothing. A single Reddit post hit 460k views , and Reddit became our number one source of paying customers. Organic search traffic grew roughly 40x , from around 700 visits a month to 27,800, and we cracked the top 3 for "best ai presentation maker" and the cluster around it. The flagship listicle alone pulled 9,496 clicks and close to 891,000 impressions in a single month. A $20 backlink system I built with a couple of agents took our Domain Rating from 21 to 36 and our backlinks from 132 to 396. From invisible to cited inside AI : 755 mentions in Grok, 212 in Google's AI Mode, 180 in AI Overviews, plus Gemini and Perplexity. Brand searches grew around 5x , and we finished 4th on Product Hunt with 314 upvotes. I raised my first PR using Claude code! A huge milestone for me since I have often had to push/drop ideas due to lack of tech bandwidth. My Most Important Learnings It wasn't all upward, and the back half of this period is where I learned the most. SEO. At the end of May we lost our ranking on "best ai presentation maker," one of our biggest keywords and the blog behind it, and June dropped off hard because of it. When that much of your traffic sits on one or two listicles, a single ranking slip takes the whole month with it. Listicles are also the most contested and most volatile pages you can try to rank for, so leaning the channel on them was the real risk. The fix, which I'd already started, was to spread the weight across detailed guides and tool pages that don't rise and fall with one blog. Reddit. In May, posting got inconsistent because we were heads-down on a big June launch, and Reddit fell off as a result. When a channel is actively driving growth, you can't go quiet on it for a few weeks without paying for it. That's what pushed me to build the proper Claude skill for Reddit, so the posting could stay consistent even when my attention was elsewhere. Backlinks. The moment I eased off the outreach, our Domain Rating stalled. Authority needs steady upkeep; it flattens out the week you stop pushing on it. There are far more channel-by-channel learnings than I can reasonably fit into one blog. If you want to get into any of it, or just compare notes, reach out: LinkedIn .
